attrs.citation: Bloomfield, Netkachova & Rushby, Defeaters and Eliminative Argumentation in Assurance 2.0, SRI-CSL-2024-01 (arXiv 2405.15800), May 2024
hypotheses: none — it is a method, not a theorem
attrs.note: READ in R5.2. Two things taken: `accepted_risk` as a terminal state distinct from elimination, and the retain-don't-delete rule, which is the direct answer to R5.1's question of what object records a defective mechanism. One correction to the audit that cited it: the rebutting/undercutting distinction is POLLOCK'S, from defeasible reasoning, not Assurance 2.0's — Assurance 2.0 adopts it. The provenance of a borrowed vocabulary is the kind of thing this ledger claims to track.
attrs.result: A defeater in an assurance case may point at a claim, an argument step, or an evidence node, and progresses through a lifecycle — open doubt, refuted by a subcase, addressed by modifying the case, or explicitly accepted as a residual risk. A resolved defeater is RETAINED as commentary rather than deleted. A defeater that reveals a flaw in the system rather than in the argument is closer to a hazard than to an argumentative doubt.

attrs.citation: Brewka, Ellmauthaler, Strass, Wallner & Woltran, Abstract Dialectical Frameworks Revisited / An Introduction to ADFs (2013–2014), arXiv:1405.0406
hypotheses: the acceptance conditions are total functions over parent states

attrs.note: GPT-5.6's warning at R7.4: do not assume Dung must be the eventual native substrate. A mosaic with TYPED support and attack, where a node's status depends on which kinds of support are present, is closer to an acceptance condition than to a bare attack relation. Dung can remain a useful derived projection.
attrs.result: ADFs generalise Dung frameworks by giving each node an ACCEPTANCE CONDITION over the states of its parents, rather than fixing the relation to be attack. Dung AFs are the special case where every condition is .

attrs.citation: J. P. Anderson, Computer Security Technology Planning Study, ESD-TR-73-51 (1972) — the reference monitor concept; the NEAT criteria as later stated
hypotheses: the mechanism mediates a defined subject/object/operation relation — the requirements are stated relative to that relation and say nothing outside it
attrs.note: The word to keep is EVALUABLE. Anderson's list already concedes that non-bypassability is discharged by evaluation of the mechanism — analysis, verification, review — and not by the mechanism reporting on itself. That is why R7.3 splits GPT-5.6's single law: the always-invoked half is checkable at admission, the non-bypassable half is an evaluation obligation.
attrs.result: A reference validation mechanism must be Non-bypassable, Evaluable and Always-invoked, and must additionally be tamperproof. These are DESIGN REQUIREMENTS on a mechanism, not properties a mechanism can test of itself.

attrs.citation: Modgil & Prakken, The ASPIC+ framework for structured argumentation: a tutorial, Argument & Computation 5 (2014); and the structured-argumentation literature that follows it
hypotheses: the argument structures and the attack typing are defined BEFORE the abstract framework is derived
a preference ordering exists to turn attacks into defeats; without one, every attack defeats
attrs.note: The available route for the 28 defeaters this artifact currently drops into `outside`: reify claim, evidence, assumption, rule and receipt into argument structures so that attacks on premises become undermining attacks on the arguments that use them. Cited for the CONSTRUCTION, not as evidence that this artifact has performed it.
attrs.result: Structured arguments are built from premises and rules, attacks are typed (undermining on premises, undercutting on rules, rebutting on conclusions), and a Dung-style ABSTRACT framework is then DERIVED for semantic evaluation. An attack becomes a defeat only through a preference ordering.

attrs.citation: Fazl Barez, Tingchen Fu, Ameya Prabhu, Stephen Casper, Amartya Sanyal, Adel Bibi, et al., "Open Problems in Machine Unlearning for AI Safety" (arXiv 2501.04952), January 2025
hypotheses: none — it is a problem survey, not a theorem
attrs.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-24 by fetching the arXiv record; author list and date check out. READ NARROWLY. It is cited for the claim that capability removal from weights is an open problem, NOT for any specific impossibility — the abstract does not assert one and this ledger does not get to upgrade a survey into a theorem.
attrs.result: Unlearning is not a comprehensive solution for AI safety. Dual-use knowledge is the central obstacle: models combine individually harmless information for harmful purposes, so unlearning that information degrades beneficial uses. Evaluation, robustness and the preservation of safety features during unlearning are named as open.

attrs.citation: Bates, Tian, Butler & Moyer, Trustworthy Whole-System Provenance for the Linux Kernel, USENIX Security 2015 — Linux Provenance Modules
hypotheses: completeness holds over the declared universe of controlled data types, and not outside it
the lower monitor's mediation is independently verified — the inheritance is only as strong as that verification
the trusted computing base is intact; disabling LPM requires booting a different kernel, which is detectable by attestation rather than prevented
attrs.note: The closest prior art to GPT-5.6's `causal-support monitor`, and it is prior art for the STRUCTURE of the argument rather than for the conclusion. Three features are the ones to copy and all three are things this artifact has been reaching for independently: completeness is stated relative to a named type universe, it is reduced to a lower verified monitor instead of asserted, and the irreducible residual is relocated to an attestation root and declared — which is exactly the shape of ASM-REMOTE-MODEL-IDENTITY.
attrs.result: The reference monitor guarantees transfer to a PROVENANCE monitor. LPM states G1 Complete as `the provenance record be gapless in its description of system activity`, scoped to CONTROLLED DATA TYPES, and discharges it by INHERITANCE: a provenance hook is placed directly beneath each LSM authorization hook, LSM's complete mediation over controlled data types has been formally verified elsewhere, and LPM therefore inherits that assurance rather than establishing it. The paper declares the resulting gap — because the provenance hook sits beneath the authorization hook, LPM cannot record FAILED access attempts — and relocates tamperproofness to secure boot and TPM attestation rather than closing it.

attrs.citation: Beeri, Fagin, Maier & Yannakakis, On the desirability of acyclic database schemes, J. ACM 30 (1983)
hypotheses: the scheme is alpha-acyclic
relations, i.e. finite instances over the scheme
attrs.result: For an acyclic database scheme, pairwise consistency of the relations implies global consistency; and the acyclic schemes are exactly those for which this holds.

attrs.citation: T. A. Budd & D. Angluin, "Two notions of correctness and their relation to testing", Acta Informatica 18(1):31–45, 1982
hypotheses: the general case: arbitrary programs over an unbounded input domain
attrs.note: REGISTERED BECAUSE IT IS THE RESULT THIS ROUND EVADES RATHER THAN THE ONE IT RELIES ON, and the distinction is the interesting part. The impact domain is finite — |P(K)| = 32 — so the complete extensional signature of a semantics on the fixture is computable, and equivalence is DECIDED by comparing signatures. That is not a refutation of Budd & Angluin and it is not a general method; it is the special case their theorem does not cover. A round that grows K, or moves to an unbounded rule language, inherits the undecidability and must go back to arguing about equivalence.
attrs.result: Deciding whether a mutant is EQUIVALENT to the original program — syntactically different, behaviourally identical — is UNDECIDABLE in general. A mutation score therefore has an unknown denominator, since surviving mutants cannot in general be partitioned into `equivalent` and `missed`.

attrs.citation: P. Cousot & R. Cousot, "Abstract interpretation: a unified lattice model for static analysis of programs by construction or approximation of fixpoints", POPL ’77, pp. 238–252
hypotheses: the abstraction is related to the concrete semantics by a Galois connection (or, more weakly, a sound concretisation)
the abstract transfer functions are monotone over a lattice satisfying the chain conditions the fixpoint argument needs
attrs.note: GPT-5.6 cited this framing to rule on R7.4 §8.1: with no trustworthy narrowing information, `typed closure = untyped reachability labelled ⊤` is the CORRECT result and not a shortfall. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: no Galois connection has been exhibited between this impact lattice and any concrete semantics of invalidation, because no concrete semantics of invalidation has been written down. The abstract side runs; the thing it abstracts is ADMISSION-SUPPORT-NONBYPASSABLE, which is open.
attrs.result: A sound static analysis deliberately OVER-APPROXIMATES the possible behaviours of a program: the analysis computes a fixpoint in an abstract lattice that safely bounds the concrete one. Loss of precision produces false alarms; omitting a possible behaviour breaks soundness. The two failure directions are not symmetric.

attrs.citation: R. A. DeMillo, R. J. Lipton & F. G. Sayward, "Hints on Test Data Selection: Help for the Practicing Programmer", Computer 11(4):34–41, April 1978
hypotheses: the mutation operators model faults a competent programmer would plausibly make
adequacy is measured against the registered mutant set, which is not claimed to be the set of all possible faults
attrs.note: GPT-5.6’s ruling on ROUND7_4_MOSAIC_BRIEF.md §8.2 named this discipline as the general form of R7.4’s question `is there a rule beyond test at singletons?`. The answer taken here: a singleton was a DISTINGUISHING INPUT for one mutant, not a privileged point. NOTE THE LIMIT THIS SOURCE IMPOSES ON THE CLAIMS CITING IT — adequacy against a registered fault model is a test-adequacy statement and is NOT promoted to a proof of semantic correctness.
attrs.result: Introduces MUTATION ANALYSIS as a test-adequacy criterion: generate plausible faulty variants of the program, and measure a suite by which non-equivalent variants it can distinguish from the original. Carries the COUPLING EFFECT conjecture — that tests distinguishing simple faults also distinguish complex ones.

attrs.citation: D. E. Denning, A Lattice Model of Secure Information Flow, CACM 19(5) (1976)
hypotheses: the class set is fixed and its order is declared before flows are certified
the join is the least upper bound — a combination is labelled at least as high as every contributor, never lower
attrs.note: The reason R7.3 refuses GPT-5.6's flat lattice. A flat lattice with one UNKNOWN token above incomparable kinds has no element for `correctness or confidentiality but not authority`, which is exactly what its own transfer example produces. P(kinds) under ⊆ with join = union is the Denning-shaped carrier, and it makes UNKNOWN = ⊤ rather than a separate token.
attrs.result: Information-flow security classes form a lattice, justified by the semantics of flow: the class of a value combined from several sources is the JOIN of their classes, and a mechanism is secure when every flow is upward in the order. The lattice structure is what permits a mechanism to be constructed and certified rather than argued case by case.

attrs.citation: Saltzer & Schroeder, The Protection of Information in Computer Systems, Proc. IEEE 63(9) (1975) — the complete mediation principle
hypotheses: an object universe is fixed before the universal is stated — the principle quantifies over `every object` and does not itself say which objects those are

The caching caveat has also already been paid here once, in a different vocabulary: R6.2's closure-label cache had to be cleared after the mutation battery or §8 and §9 would compute against stale mediation state, which is precisely `a remembered result that was not systematically updated`.

The authors note it forces a system-wide view of access control that includes initialization, recovery, shutdown and maintenance, and that proposals to cache the result of an authority check must be examined skeptically, because a change in authority requires remembered results to be systematically updated.

attrs.citation: Goodenough, Weinstock & Klein, Eliminative Argumentation: A Basis for Arguing Confidence in System Properties, CMU/SEI-2015-TR-005
hypotheses: none — it is a method, not a theorem
attrs.note: FETCHED AND READ in R5.2, not summarized from the audit. The load-bearing sentence for this project is not the taxonomy: it is 'in eliminative induction, we never speak of evidence as directly supporting a claim; it supports a claim only to the extent that it eliminates doubts associated with the claim.' That is the strongest available statement of what R5, R5.1 and R5.2 have each rediscovered one layer deeper. Cited for the vocabulary and the structural rules ONLY; the Baconian m|n confidence arithmetic is NOT adopted, because combining eliminations needs a defeater-independence argument this project does not have.
attrs.result: Confidence in a claim comes from identifying and ELIMINATING reasons to doubt it, not from accumulating positive support. An eliminative argument has five elements — claims, evidence, inference rules, defeaters, argument terminators — and there are only three kinds of defeater, determined by the element attacked: rebutting (a claim), undermining (evidence), undercutting (an inference rule). The leaves of such an argument are terminated defeaters, open defeaters, or inference rules asserted to be tautologies.

attrs.evidence: None. The ARCHITECTURAL half of GPT-5.6's law, and it cannot be enforced from inside the system it describes. GPT-5.6's operational form ends `any unmediated external observation ⇒ τ is inadmissible`; that clause presupposes the system can DETECT an unmediated observation, and if it could detect it the observation would be mediated. So it is not a runtime rule. It is the statement of the property, discharged by an argument about the execution environment or not at all — which is what SRC-ANDERSON-1972-REFMON already concedes by listing EVALUABLE beside non-bypassable. SRC-BATES-2015-LPM is the demonstration of the only route that has actually worked: do not argue the universe is closed, REDUCE it to a lower monitor whose mediation over a typed object set was independently verified, and inherit. There is a decidable shadow, weaker than the property and stronger than nothing: enumerate every exported path that performs the effect and refuse any that is not the mediator. scripts/check-mutation-surface.mjs has been doing exactly that for Ledger `bal` writes since R5.1, and its own first run flagged a comment, which is the honest summary of what a surface scan resolves.

attrs.evidence: R6.1 made `sustained` an eternal attack. DEF-DISCHARGE-PROSE-STALE is sustained because the R5.1 record really was stale — and it was fixed at R5.2, its repair is checked on every run, and it was still attacking the current assumption. That is historical truth read as present applicability, which is exactly the confusion `refutation_scope` was built for at R3.1, arriving in the assurance graph. THE ACTIVATION FUNCTION IS THE INCIDENT'S OWN CLOSURE, which is what makes it worth having rather than a policy flag: a sustained doubt is inactive exactly while its reproducer mutation is still refused, so if the old exploit starts working again the closure goes red and the doubt becomes an active attack automatically. Incident replay is the temporal activation function. §5b2 carries both controls — a closed incident does not attack, and the same doubt attacks again once it is not closed.

Dung 1995 Theorem 30: every well-founded argumentation framework has exactly one complete extension, which is also the grounded, preferred and stable one. For a finite framework, well-founded means acyclic. §9 compiles the mosaic into an abstract framework on every run, measures acyclicity, and prints the longest attack chain. The framework is acyclic today, so the four semantics coincide and no record in this tree can tell them apart. THIS IS A MEASUREMENT WITH AN EXPIRY, and R6.1 corrects how R6 stated it. Theorem 30 gives a SUFFICIENT condition for coincidence, so the first cyclic attack EXPIRES THE PROOF that the semantics agree — it does not establish that they disagree on that particular framework, and many cyclic frameworks still have all four coincide. §9 goes red on the first cycle, which stays the right conservative policy: compare the semantics explicitly or withhold the labels until one is ruled. R6 wrote that a cycle 'makes the choice observable', which is the same species of overreach this artifact keeps catching — a sufficient condition read as a biconditional.

attrs.evidence: Two steps. (1) Monotonicity carries f(∅)=1 to every superset, so every set is sufficient and the unique minimal sufficient set — the unique prime implicant — is ∅. The kernel family is {∅}. (2) A minimal revocation cut is a minimal transversal of the kernel family: a set meeting every kernel. No set meets ∅, since ∅ has no elements to meet. So no transversal exists and the cut family is empty. The consequence is not that revocation is expensive; it is that revocation by artifact deletion is not defined. scripts/emb-battery-control.mjs §2 computes both families over the declared universe and carries the POSITIVE CONTROL that makes the result mean something: CAP-SYNTHETIC-AOBC, where f(∅)=0, yields cuts {A,B} and {A,C} through the same code path. An engine returning `no cuts` for everything would produce the empty family and fail the control.

attrs.evidence: The dual of EMB-SUPPORT-GRAPH, and the formulation that makes revocation a computable question instead of a philosophical one. It is the minimal cut-set problem from reliability engineering, where a minimal cut set is a smallest combination of component failures sufficient to fail the top-level function. THE SPLIT IS THE IMPORTANT HALF: a descendant can retain the competence to do X while losing the authority to invoke X, and those are cuts through different parts of the graph. R5 collapsed both into 'revocation' and then proved, correctly and uselessly, that one of them is impossible under an absorbing-sink model. GPT-5.6's audit is also right that the absorbing-sink model was the wrong default in the first place — resource.mjs types knowledge as REUSABLE, which is the linear-logic `!` and the opposite of a consumable.

Third: MUT-EXTRACTED-RECEIPT-ALTERED is observed by a different process from check-mosaic's §5b battery, because the attack is a filesystem operation and cannot be a deep-copy registry mutation.

attrs.statement: A downloadable review artifact proves, from a bare extraction and the repository it ships, that every canonical file it contains — the head receipt included — is the exact bytes of the commit its bundle names, and that every other file is a declared build product.

attrs.evidence: FAC-ARTIFACT-CANONICAL-MATCH bound every path IN the commit and left every path outside it to a filename pattern. GPT-5.6 reproduced both consequences on a clean extraction of INV-R8.2: an invented `fake-proof-output.txt` containing arbitrary text asserting everything passed was admitted because its suffix matched `*-output.txt`, and the REAL `mosaic-gate-output.txt` was rewritten in place — bundle untouched — and also passed. Both reproduced here before the repair. A FILENAME MATCHING A BUILD-PRODUCT GLOB IS NOT A FILE THAT BUILD PRODUCED, and these are the files that look most like evidence to a human reader: captured gate output, which the archive's own front page invites a reviewer to compare against their own run. Which capture belongs to which kind was MEASURED, not assumed: all ten were re-run inside a clean extraction and diffed. Seven reproduce (one modulo the gate's own elapsed-time line, under a normalisation bounded to that one line); three do not, for three distinct reasons, each stated in its declaration. Enforced in two places that need each other: scripts/verify-review-artifact.mjs re-runs the derived commands against a real extraction, and check-mosaic §6 checks the DECLARATION shape, which is registry data and therefore portable to a tree with no git.
attrs.gap: INTERNAL CONSISTENCY, NOT AUTHENTICITY — unchanged, and inherited whole from FAC-ARTIFACT-CANONICAL-MATCH. An attacker who rewrites a capture, rebuilds the bundle and re-runs the gates passes this, because nothing is signed; FAC-RECEIPT-AUTH is that record and is open. Second, THE UNTRUSTED SET IS THE RESIDUE AND IT IS NOT EMPTY: THE UNTRUSTED SET IS NOT EMPTY and this sentence deliberately does not say how large it is — the gate derives that (brief-facts {{ARTIFACT_UNTRUSTED_COUNT}}). INV-R8.3 wrote a literal here and it was wrong, and the honest statement is that they are labelled rather than checked. Third, `factory-scope-output.txt` is the sharpest of them — it is a capture of a run against the SOURCE tree and it ships inside an artifact with two more narrative paths than it reports, so it was never wrong about the tree it measured and it accompanies a different one. Making it derivable means running the classifier after staging rather than before, which changes what the build does and is not attempted here. Fourth: a `derived` declaration could in principle name a command that reads the shipped capture, which would compare a file to itself; nothing mechanical refuses that yet.
attrs.implementation_binding: scripts/verify-review-artifact.mjs — the classified-additions section and --selftest; scripts/check-mosaic.mjs — P.artifactAdditionsTyped and mutations MUT-ARTIFACT-*
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R8.2, §artifact. The derived/untrusted split is the two options that audit named. The re-derivation half is what reproducible-build verification does — rebuild and compare rather than trust a label — narrowed here to build products of a single archive.
attrs.review_focus: Two questions. (1) The re-derivation composes with the canonical check rather than duplicating it — the gate being re-run is itself a committed path already byte-compared, so an attacker cannot make capture and generator agree by editing the generator. Is that composition actually closed, or is there an ordering in which it is not? (2) `untrusted_capture` is an honest label and also a hole: nothing mechanical stops a future product being declared untrusted BECAUSE re-deriving it is inconvenient. The non-consumption rule is the only enforcement, and it constrains what may rest on such a file without constraining how many there may be.
attrs.statement: Every file in a review extraction that is NOT a byte of the canonical commit is admitted by exact name and declares a kind: a `derived` product carries the command that produced it and is re-run and compared here, and an `untrusted_capture` is declared not-evidence, states what the extraction lacks, and may not be reached by any derivation.

attrs.evidence: The alternative to quarantine is deletion, and deletion of an incident's only witness is how the incident gets rediscovered. INV-R6.1 and INV-R6.2 remain in mosaic/receipts/ byte-for-byte and remain readable; mosaic/factory.json records their state, the incident (INC-R62-MIXED-LINEAGE) and why; refs/heads/invariant-quarantine holds the exact artifact GPT-5.6 audited. check-lineage §4 refuses a head whose ancestry contains a quarantined revision and refuses a head whose own declared state is not `canonical`; factory-station.mjs verify refuses a canonical ref that has the quarantine commit as an ancestor by any route. MUT-RECOVERED-BRANCH-IS-CANONICAL is the standing attack. HEREDITY WAS ADDED AT INV-R8.1 BECAUSE A LIVE INSTANCE APPEARED. While INV-R8-RECOVERY was being built in an isolated worktree, a fourth round — INV-R7.1 — was written straight into the shared tree between 17:17 and 17:28 on 2026-08-24: 150 claims, nine established, its own receipt, verdict `promote`, and every one of its gates green in the tree it was written into. Its declared parent is the quarantined INV-R6.2. Nothing about that round is wrong on its own terms and it still cannot be canonical, because marking it so would launder its quarantined ancestor back onto the line through it. MUT-QUARANTINE-NOT-HEREDITARY is the standing attack; the round itself is preserved on refs/heads/invariant-unpromoted-r71 and recorded in mosaic/factory.json §revisions as `unpromoted`. NARROWED AT INV-R8.2, per GPT-5.6. INV-R8.1 made quarantine hereditary as such, which is more than the INV-R7.1 case proves. What it proves is that quarantine caused by invalid transition LINEAGE is hereditary with respect to ancestry, because a merge would place the poisoned ancestor back on the canonical line — a future `these tests fail` hold is repairable by a descendant and must not exile it. mosaic/factory.json now declares `quarantine_classes`, the gate reads the class rather than the state, and a class the registry does not declare is a refusal rather than a default. MUT-QUARANTINE-CLASS-UNDECLARED.
attrs.gap: The quarantine STATE is writable JSON, like everything else here — un-quarantining a revision is a one-line edit, and the only thing that would notice is a reader. That is FAC-RECEIPT-AUTH again, one level up, and it is not fixed. `unreceipted` (INV-R7) is a third state and a weaker one: there is no receipt to quarantine, only a name that will never be used. A THIRD STATE was needed and is weaker than the other two: `unpromoted` means a round exists, was never offered to a station, and has not been adjudicated by anyone. It is not a verdict on the work — INV-R7.1 looks like good work — it is a statement that no promotion protocol ever saw it. The two-axis record for INV-R7.1 (`promotion_state` + `lineage_blocked_by`) is deliberately the SMALLEST thing that says both facts. The full product schema — receipt_state x promotion_state x canonicality x ancestry_integrity x adjudication_state — is not built, because building an ontology before the cases that need it is the move this lane keeps refusing.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R6.2, §11. Assurance 2.0's instruction, which this ledger already follows for defeaters: retain a resolved item as commentary rather than deleting it.
attrs.statement: A revision whose transition identity is unsound is marked quarantined with its incident, its reason and its CLASS, keeps its receipt bytes unedited, and may never be an ancestor of the canonical head or become the head. Heredity is a property of the CLASS: a quarantine for invalid transition lineage travels with ancestry; one for a repairable content defect does not.

attrs.evidence: INV-R6.2 placed this mechanism in "whatever plays the role of the station" and shipped a checker instead, on the reasoning that a gate running after both writes have landed is reading the crime scene. The reasoning is right and the conclusion did not follow: `git update-ref <ref> <new-oid> <old-oid>` updates a ref only after verifying it still holds the expected old OID, which is the promotion predicate exactly. scripts/factory-station.mjs is `head` / `open` / `promote --expect` / `verify` over refs/heads/invariant-canonical. INV-R8-RECOVERY was produced in an isolated worktree opened at the canonical head and promoted through the compare-and-swap; MUT-STALE-PARENT-PROMOTION advances the ref underneath a candidate and watches the promotion be refused.
attrs.gap: IT CANNOT BIND A SESSION THAT DOES NOT CALL IT, and nothing at this layer can — the canonical state is the ref, and the shared working directory remains writable by anyone. Measured during this round rather than argued: a third concurrent session rewrote mosaic/embodiment.json in the shared tree at 17:17 on 2026-08-24, twenty minutes after INV-R6.2's receipt was written. `verify --worktree` names the divergence; it does not prevent it. Multi-ref promotion would need git's `update-ref --stdin` transaction mode and one ref does not. MEASURED AGAIN, AND WORSE, AT INV-R8.1: the shared tree does not hold a stray edit, it holds a COMPLETE alternative successor. Two branches from INV-R6 — {INV-R6.1 -> INV-R6.2 -> INV-R7.1} and INV-R8-RECOVERY — each pass every gate they run, and neither is wrong about itself. That is the invariant failing in real time, in the hour after the audit that named it, and it is the sharpest available statement of why local correctness does not compose into an identified global successor. CORRECTED AT INV-R8.2, and the correction is a retraction. INV-R8.1 added the rule `a head may be amended until something consumes it` and used it five times. It is false: a successful compare-and-swap on the canonical ref is itself a publication event, so `not known to be consumed` was standing in for `known not to have been consumed`. FAC-PROMOTION-FINALITY replaces it and INC-R81-PREMATURE-PROMOTION records what it cost.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R6.2, §12. git-update-ref(1); optimistic concurrency control; the compare-and-swap discipline of a distributed version-control push.
attrs.statement: A round may be promoted only by atomically advancing the canonical ref from the exact parent OID the round started from to the candidate OID. A candidate whose base has moved is refused, and must rebase, abandon, or declare an explicit merge.

attrs.evidence: Fable 5's identity walk printed `NON-CANON INV-R6`, and INV-R6 is the verified-good canonical revision that INV-R8-RECOVERY was deliberately forked from — a git ancestor of the whole recovery chain. GPT-5.6 ruled the label false and the distinction load-bearing: chain membership and historical canonicality are different predicates, and collapsing them would have written `non-canonical` onto the one revision the recovery trusted. The separate predicates are on_post_recovery_receipt_chain, on_current_canonical_git_ancestry, historically_promoted, current_head, quarantined, unpromoted.
attrs.gap: THE ROOT IS A DECLARATION, not a derivation. Nothing computes that INV-R8-RECOVERY is where OID-binding begins; it is where this factory started recording parent.commit_oid, and a reader has to take the registry's word for the boundary. Second: the predicates above are named here and only two of them are mechanised (chain membership, and quarantine heredity in check-lineage §4); `historically_promoted` has no checker, so a claim about a pre-recovery revision's standing is still prose.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's adjudication §2.1 and §14, correcting the Fable R8.3 witness.
attrs.review_focus: Is `OUTSIDE_POST_RECOVERY_CHAIN` the right predicate name, and is the pre-recovery boundary declared in the one place a reader would look?
attrs.statement: The receipt-OID identity chain roots at INV-R8-RECOVERY. A revision outside that chain is OUTSIDE_POST_RECOVERY_CHAIN, which is a statement about chain membership and not about canonicality.

attrs.evidence: FOUR occurrences of one class, and the fourth landed in the round that shipped this claim. The R4 brief said `60 records` over a 62-record ledger; the R7.2 brief said `21 sustained defeaters` where the gate printed 22; INV-R8.3 said `four files ship` over six declared untrusted captures; and INV-R9 typed `PROVED 15, OPEN 7, DECLARED 6, KNOWN 3, PROVISIONAL 2, REFUTED 2` into FAC-INTEGRATION-READJUDICATE while describing 34 imports — a histogram that sums to 35, because the fifteenth PROVED candidate is the one disposed as already_present. THE MECHANISM IS THREE PARTS AND THEIR SCOPE IS NOW STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. (a) mosaic/derived/brief-facts.json is DERIVED by check-mosaic §13 and the bundle substitutes {{KEY}} from it, refusing a bare integer before a declared noun in a source brief — this covers BRIEFS and the keys someone thought to derive. (b) check-mosaic §7 matches counted phrases in the ledger’s prose — a backstop over a fixed phrase list. (c) INV-R9.2 adds derivation at the point of use for two more surfaces: check-integration §histogram computes every status histogram from the bucket records and refuses one typed into an integration claim’s prose, and check-lineage §8 derives transition scope and refuses a receipt stating its own. NOTHING COVERS PROSE IN GENERAL.
attrs.gap: THE CLAIM AS ORIGINALLY WORDED — `no count of a registry-derivable quantity is typed into prose` — IS FALSIFIED BY ITS OWN ROUND and is not what the mechanism enforces. What is enforced is: brief text through substitution; the ledger prose a fixed phrase list reaches; integration status histograms; receipt transition scope. A count phrased outside those four surfaces passes, and the R9 histogram is the proof — it was in a ledger field, and §7’s phrase list did not contain that shape, because a phrase list contains the drifts someone has already thought of. THE HONEST FORM OF THE RULE IS NEGATIVE — prose should not state a derivable count at all — and deciding whether a sentence states a cardinality is the definitional-subsumption problem this ledger declined to mechanise at INV-R6. A HISTORICAL count must also stay a literal (`R7.1 counted 21 repaired defects` is a fact about a past state), so the lint carries an as-of form, and every count in this evidence field about a PAST artifact is one of those.
attrs.implementation_binding: scripts/check-mosaic.mjs — P.ledgerProseCounts (§7) and the §13 brief-facts derivation
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's adjudication of the Fable R8.3 pass, §9: adopt the rule, not the regex implementation — prefer structured fields and generated sentences; a heuristic prose checker may be a backstop, not the source of truth. The two mechanisms this claim names were built on the R7.x lane and arrived here through the INV-R9 content integration.
attrs.review_focus: The claim is about an ORDERING between two mechanisms, not about either one. Is `structured field first, phrase match second` actually what the code does, or does the phrase list still carry weight the structured half should? And: the R8.3 drift was found by an outside reader on a shipped artifact, not by either mechanism — is there a class of count that neither half can reach in principle?
attrs.statement: No count of a registry-derivable quantity is typed into prose ON A SURFACE THIS MECHANISM COVERS: brief text, ledger prose the phrase list reaches, integration status histograms, and receipt transition scope. The quantity is computed where it is printed, or stated as a derived key the build substitutes; a phrase-matching check over prose is a backstop and never the source of truth.

attrs.evidence: scripts/check-derivation.mjs builds the read-to-writer graph from mosaic/factory.json's artifact_additions and refuses on multiple writers, self-read or cycle, with a positive control that admits the real registry and prints its topological order. Fable 5's witness established the refusals; this is that check over the shipped registry rather than a fixture.

evidence_qualifiers.population: every derived build product declared in mosaic/factory.json artifact_additions — a finite enumerated set, so exhaustion is the right kind and not a stand-in for a proof about all possible registries

attrs.gap: A GRAPH PROPERTY AND NOTHING MORE, and the distance between this and reproducibility is the point of FAC-DERIVATION-CLOSED. Acyclicity gives schedulability: a topological order exists and re-derivation terminates. It does not give determinism, confluence or evidential force — a single-node registry running `date +%s%N > out.txt` is single-writer, self-read-free and acyclic, and produces different bytes on every run. That counterexample ships as a permanent falsifier.
attrs.prior_art: Fable 5 ARTIFACT_DERIVATION.md; GPT-5.6 adjudication §7, which accepted the graph half and rejected the evidence half. The separation is the one reproducible-build practice and SLSA already draw between build-graph shape and hermeticity.
attrs.review_focus: The claim deliberately stops at the graph. Is the declared reads set actually the material input set for each product, or only the part someone wrote down? That question is FAC-DERIVATION-CLOSED and is open.
attrs.statement: The build-product derivation registry declares reads and writes per product, and admissibility is a graph property: exactly one declared writer per path, no product reading its own output, and an acyclic read-to-writer graph admitting a topological order.

attrs.evidence: NOT ESTABLISHED, and the falsifiers are shipped so that it cannot be assumed. scripts/check-derivation.mjs --falsifiers builds three registries that satisfy FAC-DERIVATION-ACYCLIC completely and fail to reproduce: a clock-dependent command, an RNG-dependent command, and a command whose real input is an undeclared environment variable. Each is admitted by the graph check and each produces different bytes or different output on a second run. The artifact's own derived products are re-run and compared by scripts/verify-review-artifact.mjs, which is a weaker and honest empirical fact: they reproduced on this machine, under this toolchain, at this moment.
attrs.gap: EVERY CLAUSE IS UNDONE. Nothing declares a material-input set beyond the argv; the toolchain is recorded as a provenance string in the receipt and is not pinned or verified; environment is scrubbed with `env -i` at verification time and is not declared per product; no product declares a nondeterminism policy. The re-derivation check in verify-review-artifact.mjs would pass a product that is reproducible only because nobody changed the machine.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6 adjudication §7, rejecting Fable's PROOFS.md P3 as stated. SLSA build levels and reproducible-builds practice treat hermeticity and reproducibility as requirements distinct from build-graph shape.
attrs.review_focus: The falsifiers prove acyclicity is insufficient. What is the smallest declaration that would make one real product in this registry hermetic enough to carry evidential force — and is that even the right target, or should derived products be typed as non-hermetic evidence and consumed accordingly?
attrs.statement: A derived product carries reproducible evidential force only when all material inputs are declared and content-bound, the transitive toolchain and runtime are pinned, environment inputs are declared or neutralised, network and mutable references are blocked or recorded under an explicit non-hermetic evidence type, and nondeterminism is eliminated, seeded, normalised or explicitly modelled.

attrs.evidence: scripts/check-publication-identity.mjs walks the chain from one ref read and compares against refs/tags/*. The measurement was first made by Fable 5 on the INV-R8.3 chain (4 revisions), independently reproduced by GPT-5.6 against the shipped bundle, and re-runs here at every head. Tags outside the chain — drafts, the quarantine head, the unpromoted R7.1 snapshot — are reported as OUTSIDE_POST_RECOVERY_CHAIN rather than as non-canonical, per FAC-CHAIN-ROOT.

evidence_qualifiers.population: every promoted revision on the post-recovery receipt chain at the current head, and every ref under refs/tags in the canonical repository

attrs.gap: A MEASUREMENT OF THE CURRENT CHAIN AND OF LIGHTWEIGHT TAGS. The tags in this repository are lightweight refs, so the mapping they carry is exactly a name-to-OID pair and is therefore derivable. An annotated or signed tag carries a tag OBJECT with a message, a tagger and possibly a signature, none of which is derivable from the receipt chain — so this result does not extend to a future annotated tag, and FAC-TAG-DERIVED states that scope explicitly.

attrs.evidence: Kohli 2026 ('Nine Judges, Two Effective Votes', arXiv 2605.29800, submitted 28 May 2026) measures nine frontier models across three natural-language-inference datasets and reports the panel at roughly two independent votes' worth of information, quantified with Kish effective sample size against a Condorcet null. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY this round rather than taken on the audit's word. It is a precedent for the METHOD and not a constant to transplant: this loop's panel is three models, not nine, on a task distribution that is not natural-language inference. UNMEASURED HERE. What the result licenses today is one negative: three concurring models is not three votes, and mosaic/evidence.json types such concurrence as `model_judgment`, which discharges plausibility and nothing else.
attrs.gap: No probe set exists. Running this needs known-answer items the three models have not seen, which is a real design problem and not a scheduling one.

attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6’s INV-R9.2 audit §5, and it is the sharper half of the ruling. INV-R9 disposed of RECEIPT-BINDS-IMPORT-CLOSURE — PROVED on the source lane — as already_present under FAC-RECEIPT-EVIDENCE-CLOSED, which is DECLARED here. Even had the subsumption been discharged, a broader DECLARED proposition does not make a narrower PROVED result redundant: the source proof establishes something the declaration does not. So the candidate was being discarded in favour of a weaker record and nothing noticed, because the gate compared propositions and never compared assurance. check-integration now refuses an already_present whose source status is settled and whose canonical target is not — MUT-INTEGRATION-ASSURANCE-INVERTED, run against a declared synthetic control because INV-R9.3 withdrew the only production record.
attrs.gap: THE IMPLEMENTED CHECK IS A COARSE SHADOW OF THE CLAIM. It compares settled-vs-unsettled and nothing finer, because this ledger has no order over statuses and inventing one would be a much larger ruling than the case needed — GPT-5.6 said explicitly not to. So PROVED-under-KNOWN, MEASURED-under-CONDITIONAL and every other pair inside the settled band pass unexamined. What is OPEN is the general relation; what is enforced is the one inversion that actually occurred.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6’s INV-R9.2 audit §5. Related: INV-R7.4’s declared-versus-discharged ladder, which is the proposition half of the same problem.
attrs.review_focus: Is a total order over statuses actually needed, or is the right object a partial order in which only some pairs are comparable and the rest force adjudication?
attrs.statement: A source claim is redundant under an existing target proposition only when the target BOTH semantically covers the source proposition AND carries target-lane assurance sufficient for the covered proposition. Proposition dominance is not assurance dominance.

attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6’s INV-R9.2 audit §7, measured against the implementation. scripts/integration-delta.mjs already computes dropped_ids and removed_files; nothing consumes them. candidatePopulation disposes candidate_ids only and filePopulation changed_files only, so a source deletion is not a candidate and not a file disposition. The collision test reads pL.has(k) && pL.get(k) !== baseline, so a canonical DELETION of a shared record is not a dual-lane change. For the INV-R7.5 instance every one of these is zero, which is why the instance stands — and zero is exactly why nobody noticed.
attrs.gap: NOT IMPLEMENTED, and deliberately not implemented here. The full deletion algebra needs a disposition vocabulary of its own (a deletion may be adopted, refused, or collide with a target modification) and INV-R9.3 was scoped to close the two blockers before Phase D. This must close before the NEXT cross-lane integration, which is Δ(next frozen R7.x − INV-R7.5), and that delta will not be all-additions.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6’s INV-R9.2 audit §7.
attrs.review_focus: Is a deletion a disposition of the SOURCE’s act, or of the TARGET’s decision not to keep something? The two give different vocabularies.
attrs.statement: An integration disposition domain must cover source-lane and canonical-lane DELETIONS — dropped claim records, removed paths, and delete-versus-modify collisions — not only additions and modifications.

assumptions: the pinned materials are the artifacts the review read (their bytes are verified; the reading is not)
the substrate executed the check as written (ASM-SUBSTRATE-INTEGRITY)
attrs.evidence: INV-R9’s gate compared `candidate_count` to the sum of the bucket lengths — two fields of one document, both written by one author. Setting the count to 2 and truncating the buckets to match removed 33 of 35 candidates from the record with the gate still printing `every candidate is accounted for`; that mutation is registered as MUT-INTEGRATION-COUNT-AND-BUCKETS-TRIMMED and is refused. scripts/integration-delta.mjs locates each material BY CONTENT (a file whose name matches and whose bytes do not is reported as a mismatch and not used), unpacks the two review artifacts and the predecessor commit, and derives: 141 baseline claims → 176 source claims, 35 candidates, 8 shared records the source lane changed, 0 records changed by BOTH lanes, 0 candidates already present in the predecessor, 49 changed paths, 0 removed paths. Every one of those figures matches what INV-R9 asserted and what GPT-5.6 recomputed independently: the integration content was correct, and until now it was unfalsifiable. The derivation ships as mosaic/derived/integration-delta.json (kind: derived) and `node scripts/integration-delta.mjs` re-runs it and byte-compares. AND THE GATE DISTINGUISHES RECORDED FROM RE-DERIVED. The committed derivation says its materials were verified, which is a fact about the machine that generated it; INV-R9.2’s own pre-promotion simulation caught this gate trusting that field in a clean extraction where the ZIPs are absent — printing `sha256 verified` and running every derived check against a JSON file nothing had re-derived, which is the round’s defect one layer out. The materials are now located AT GATE TIME, by content, against the hashes the manifest pins. In a materials-free extraction the gate reports RECORDED, NOT RE-DERIVED and 8 checks NOT STATED.

coverage.domain: the claim-record and file deltas between the pinned source and baseline artifacts
coverage.enumerator: scripts/integration-delta.mjs over the two content-addressed artifacts and the predecessor commit

evidence_qualifiers.population: every candidate record and every changed path in every integration manifest

attrs.gap: THE MATERIALS ARE OUTSIDE THE CANONICAL BOUNDARY AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. A quarantined lane’s artifact must not enter canonical source, so the two review ZIPs are evidence attachments and not committed. Where they are absent — a clean extraction, a machine without them — every derived check reports NOT STATED and the gate says how many. An absent input is never a pass, but neither is it a proof, so this claim is established HERE and re-establishable THERE only by an auditor who has the artifacts whose hashes this file pins. Second, and it is the honest reading of the above: in the shipped artifact this claim is NOT STATED, because nothing there can re-run the derivation. It is established where the materials are and re-establishable where they are brought. Third: `changed_files` is compared by content hash with no normalization, so CLAIM_LEDGER.json is always reported changed because its `_round` pointer always differs — the disposition record carries the reason, and a normalization that hid it would be the defect this lane has chased since INV-R5.1.
attrs.prior_art: in-toto (Torres-Arias, Afzali, Kuppusamy, Curtmola & Cappos, USENIX Security 2019) names the missing structure exactly: a step emits LINK metadata recording the MATERIALS it consumed and the PRODUCTS it emitted, each bound by hash, and the LAYOUT is what makes the products answerable to the materials. INV-R9 recorded materials and asserted products. Read narrowly: in-toto’s layouts are SIGNED and this artifact has no signature — FAC-RECEIPT-AUTH is still open — so what is borrowed is the materials/products shape, not the authentication.
attrs.review_focus: Is `derivable: none` an honest state, or does shipping a committed derivation that most verifiers cannot re-run amount to a self-report with extra steps?
attrs.statement: An integration manifest’s candidate population and file delta are RECOMPUTED from the content-addressed materials it pins, and the authored dispositions are checked against that recomputation by set membership. A manifest may not be the only account of the delta it disposes of.

attrs.evidence: Lineage relies on prior receipt CONTENTS — `invariants.before` is checked against the parent's `after`, and the delta is computed against the parent's manifest — while nothing bound those contents. A parent receipt is writable JSON; editing one after its child was written left every gate green. A child cannot hash itself, but it can hash every parent, which turns the chain into a content-linked history without waiting for signatures. MUT-PARENT-RECEIPT-EDIT alters a parent receipt and leaves the child untouched, and check-lineage §5 refuses.
attrs.gap: This is content-linking, NOT authentication. Nothing signs a receipt, nothing timestamps one, and an editor who changes a parent may simply update the child's recorded digest too — the chain then remains internally consistent and says nothing about who wrote it or when. That is FAC-RECEIPT-AUTH and it is open. The binding is worth having anyway: it makes an isolated edit fail loudly, which is the common case.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R6.2, §9. Hash chaining, as in a Merkle-linked log; in-toto link chains verified against an intended sequence.
attrs.statement: A child receipt binds the sha256 of its parent receipt's bytes, so the chain of named JSON files is content-linked and a parent edited after its child breaks verification.

attrs.evidence: INV-R8.1 promoted and then force-tagged one revision id through five further canonical commits, on a rule it stated itself: A HEAD MAY BE AMENDED UNTIL SOMETHING CONSUMES IT. GPT-5.6 refuted the premise in a line that generalises — NOT KNOWN TO BE CONSUMED IS NOT KNOWN NOT TO HAVE BEEN CONSUMED. A successful CAS on the canonical ref IS a publication event: any reader anywhere observes the ref the instant it advances, and no consumer registry exists that could establish otherwise. It is the same epistemic substitution this ledger has eliminated at five other layers, made about its own history by the round that built the mechanism. `git tag -f` is removed from scripts/factory-station.mjs; a promotion whose revision id already names a commit is refused BEFORE the ref advances, which is where the first version of this check was not. The selftest creates an id, fails to move it, and then creates a fresh id as the positive control.
attrs.gap: ENFORCED FROM INV-R8.2 AND NOT BEFORE. The six INV-R8.1 commits and their tags stay exactly as they are — retroactive enforcement over immutable history is how you edit the past to satisfy the present — so the artifact permanently contains six canonical commits under one revision id, and INC-R81-PREMATURE-PROMOTION is the record of why. Second: the rule constrains what a station may do to the ref; it does not stop a promotion of an UNFINISHED candidate, which is the actual mistake underneath. `finished` is not a mechanical property and this claim does not pretend to make it one. Third: nothing prevents a session from running `git tag -f` by hand — the refusal is in the station, not in the repository.

attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R8.1, §4. SLSA Source v1.2: a source revision is a logically immutable snapshot. git-tag(1): use a new tag name once an old one could have been observed, because otherwise two consumers hold different content under one version name.
attrs.statement: Every successful compare-and-swap that advances the canonical ref creates a new immutable source revision. A revision id, once it names a canonical commit, may never be moved. Drafts are amendable; a correction after promotion is a new revision id.

attrs.evidence: INV-R8.2 made promotion final and published across two separate git ref transactions — compare-and-swap the canonical branch, then `git tag` the revision id. GPT-5.6 reproduced the split: with the tag absent at the check, the CAS succeeds, an interleaved writer creates the revision id against another commit, and `git tag` then fails, leaving the canonical branch at the candidate while the revision identity names a stranger. A crash between the two commands leaves the analogous canonical-but-untagged state. Either way the successor is VISIBLE TO EVERY READER before its identity exists, and the refusal fires after the thing it refuses has happened — which is the defect INV-R8.2 corrected one layer up and reintroduced one layer down. Repair: `git update-ref --stdin` in start/prepare/commit form carries `update <ref> <new> <expected-old>` and `create refs/tags/<id> <new>` in a single transaction; git locks every ref at prepare and moves none unless all locks hold. Reproduced in both directions before and after (scripts/factory-station.mjs selftest, MUT-PUBLICATION-TAG-RACE and MUT-PUBLICATION-HEAD-RACE), each paired with the SUPERSEDED two-step sequence on identical inputs as a differential control.
attrs.gap: ATOMIC WITHIN ONE REPOSITORY, WHICH IS THE ONLY PLACE THE CANONICAL STATE LIVES — but git ref transactions are atomic per repository, so a future factory whose canonical state spanned two repositories, or a repository plus an index, would need a protocol this claim does not supply. Second, and unchanged from FAC-CANONICAL-HEAD-CAS: this binds a session that CALLS the station. It cannot bind one that writes the shared directory and never promotes. Third: `create` refuses a revision id that exists, so the id space is the boundary of identity here — two factories sharing a repository and a naming scheme would collide correctly, two using different schemes would not collide at all.
attrs.implementation_binding: scripts/factory-station.mjs — publish() and the promote path; the differential control is in selftest
attrs.prior_art: git-update-ref(1), transactional mode: refs are locked at `prepare` with their expected values and the transaction aborts rather than partially committing. GPT-5.6 named the primitive in its audit of INV-R8.2. The property is the one SLSA Source v1.2 assumes when it treats a revision as a logically immutable snapshot — a snapshot whose identity is assigned after publication was, for a window, a different object under the same name.
attrs.review_focus: The claim is about a COMPOSITION, not a primitive. INV-R8.2's selftest proved `git update-ref` compares before it swaps and `git tag` refuses to move an existing tag — both true, both still true, and neither able to observe this defect, because the defect was in the order `promote` called them. Is `publish()` now the only path by which either ref moves, and is the differential control the right shape for a repair — running the superseded implementation on identical inputs and asserting it produces the split state?
attrs.statement: Publishing a canonical successor and establishing its immutable revision identity is ONE all-or-none factory operation: either the canonical ref advances AND the revision id is created for that exact commit, or neither ref moves.

attrs.evidence: Fable 5 reconstructed the full promoted revision-name to OID mapping for the post-recovery chain from one read of refs/heads/invariant-canonical, walking parent.commit_oid through committed receipts, and GPT-5.6 independently reproduced it against the shipped INV-R8.3 bundle. scripts/check-publication-identity.mjs re-runs that walk at every head. The reader protocol matters and is part of the claim: git's multi-ref transaction is all-or-none in what it COMMITS, but a concurrent reader may still observe a subset of the changed refs, so a reader that combines a branch read with a tag read can see a mixed snapshot. Under the one-ref protocol subset visibility can stale a convenience index and cannot produce two identities for an OID already read.
attrs.gap: CONTENT-INTEGRITY-BOUND AND SELF-IDENTIFYING FROM THE OID HANDLE — NOT SELF-AUTHENTICATING, and the wrong word was in the Fable witness's own conclusion. A git OID content-binds an object under the hash assumption. It does not establish who produced it, whether the canonical ref was rolled back, whether an attacker replaced the whole repository or bundle, or whether the head is fresh. Those are FAC-RECEIPT-AUTH and remain open. Second, the minimality half is scoped to THIS publication interface: in a pull-based git design exposing a moving current head, one mutable canonical ref suffices for identity discovery — an append-only publication log or out-of-band immutable OID delivery is a counter-design, so the universal form Fable proposed is not claimed. Third: this is a PROTOCOL theorem, not a git theorem, and it binds only readers who follow the protocol.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's adjudication §2 and §3. SLSA Source v1.2 on logically immutable source revisions; git-update-ref(1) on committed-versus-observed ref state.
attrs.review_focus: The claim now rests on a declared observer protocol. Is the protocol stated precisely enough that a reader can tell whether they are following it — and is there anything in this artifact that reads a tag to establish identity?
attrs.statement: From the chain root onward the factory treats the canonical commit OID plus the committed receipt as authoritative source identity: a reader takes ONE ref read, uses the returned OID as an immutable handle, and derives revision identity from committed content without consulting the tag namespace.

attrs.evidence: MEASURED across all 17 receipts. TWO DISTINCT DEFECTS shared the block. COPY: INV-R8.3, INV-R9 and INV-R9.1 each ship lineage.parent_ids [“INV-R8.1-CONCURRENCY-OBSERVED”] beside a `parent` field naming INV-R8.2, INV-R8.3 and INV-R9 respectively — wrong when written, carried forward by copy, and the chain starts at INV-R8.3, one round earlier than the audit that found it located it. Their `rollback_target` is stale by the same route, and INV-R9.1’s reconstruction still owes “INV-R7.1’s content, replayed onto this head” in the receipt of the round that integrated it. SNAPSHOT: four receipts list one unpromoted revision where the registry now holds five — each was CORRECT when written, and a snapshot of mutable state inside an immutable record is not at risk of going stale, it is guaranteed to, and under FAC-PROMOTION-FINALITY it cannot be repaired in place. The same rule reaches scope prose: three receipts say “Nothing else” beside a DERIVED tree_delta of 10, 9 and 8 paths. check-lineage §8 derives all of it, prints it, and from INV-R9.2 refuses a receipt carrying a derivable lineage field or stating its own scope in prose.
attrs.gap: THE PHRASE TEST IS A BACKSTOP AND THE WEAKER HALF, exactly as FAC-COUNT-DERIVED says of §7. Deciding whether a sentence states a scope is the same undecidable problem as deciding whether it states a cardinality; the four patterns matched here are the ones already observed. THE PRIMARY REPAIR IS REMOVAL — INV-R6.2’s ruling when `_round` became a pointer: there is no reason for a second account to exist, and render-and-compare would hide the duplicate rather than remove it. Second: the rule is ENFORCED_FROM INV-R9.2 and the earlier receipts keep their drift, because a new invariant cannot bind immutable history; nine notes print every run and none of them fails. THIRD, AND MEASURED ON THIS ROUND’S OWN RECEIPT: the phrase test cannot distinguish USE from MENTION. The first draft of INV-R9.2’s transition.candidate quoted INV-R9.1’s `Nothing else` in order to name the defect, and the gate refused it — correctly by its own rule and wrongly as a matter of meaning. The quotation moved to transition.why, which is not scanned. That is not a repair; it is where a pattern list stops, and it is the second reason the primary mechanism is REMOVAL of the field rather than matching of its contents.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6’s INV-R9 audit §§9–10, which found the stale block on two receipts and the false transition sentence on one.
attrs.review_focus: The SNAPSHOT half generalises past receipts: any immutable record that embeds the current state of a mutable registry has this defect. Does the artifact hold others?
attrs.statement: A transition receipt keeps no second, independently writable account of its own ancestry or of its own scope. Parentage, rollback target, revision states and delta size are derived from the authoritative fields, the registry and the repository, and a receipt written under the rule may not carry them.

attrs.evidence: R5's receipt used 16-hex truncated digests and no signatures — adequate for accidental-drift detection, which is what it was for, and not a provenance boundary. R5.1 moves to full sha256 because that costs nothing; the rest is genuinely open. What is NOT done: no signing, no content-addressed receipt id, no external root of trust, and the evaluator identities in the receipt are strings anyone with write access can type. The word 'immutable' has been removed from the receipt's own description of itself.
attrs.prior_art: in-toto: signed layouts define authorized functionaries, and signed link metadata binds commands, materials and products for later chain verification. SLSA v1.2 Build and Source tracks.
attrs.statement: A receipt that becomes a trust boundary needs full content digests, a content-addressed id, and a signature or an external append-only authority; nothing writable and unsigned may be called immutable in a security sense.

attrs.evidence: R5 already declared its receipt non-decisive and said why. GPT-5.6 sharpened what decisive would mean, and the sharpening matters: today the gate checks that `decision.verdict` is a member of {promote, reject, quarantine, rollback}, which validates the SHAPE of a candidate-supplied answer. In the decisive form the verdict does not appear in the input at all — the function verifies digests and refs, evaluates the hard constraints, applies the selection policy, records which checks ran, and emits verdict and receipt atomically. Then there is no second representation to drift. NOT BUILT, and deliberately not faked: mosaic/receipts/INV-R5.1.json carries honesty.decisive = false.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6, round-5 Mosaic audit §9. in-toto's layout + signed link metadata is the mature shape for the provenance half.
attrs.statement: A decisive receipt is the OUTPUT of one admission function — adjudicate(candidate, inputs) -> (verdict, receipt) — not a document written after a gate ran and checked for a well-formed verdict field.

attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6's reproduction against the finished INV-R6.2 artifact. `EMB-CUT-EMPTY` and `EMB-BATTERY-SPLIT` are both PROVED and both rest on scripts/emb-battery-control.mjs. That file appears in no receipt manifest and in no `gates_run`. Modifying it so its final failure exit can never fire, and leaving the receipt untouched, left `check-mosaic`, `check-lineage` and `check-claim-ledger` all exiting 0. A receipt that promotes a claim without binding the bytes of its proof is not describing the evidence state it promoted. THE CLOSURE WALKER IS NOT NEW TO THIS ARTIFACT: make-invariant-review-bundle.sh has computed the transitive import closure of every named witness since round 2.1, when the archive shipped test/laws.mjs beside one of the twelve modules it imports and existsSync reported true the whole time. It was used to decide what to COPY INTO THE ZIP and never to decide what to BIND. scripts/factory-scope.mjs is that same walk pointed at the manifest, and the manifest went from 23 paths to the derived closure.
attrs.gap: DECLARED rather than PROVED, and three gaps are load-bearing. (1) The import walk is STATIC: a dynamic `import()` with a computed specifier is invisible to it, which is DEF-REPRO-DYNAMIC-IMPORT and no witness in the tree uses one. (2) Closure covers what the registries REFERENCE; a proof that lives only in a human's head, or in an evidence file no record names, is outside it by construction. (3) The `scripts/`, `AmpersandBoxDesign/` and `opensentience.org/` roots are closure-only rather than walk-closed, because those directories are shared with other lanes in the source tree; a factory file that no derivation reaches is caught only by the git-tree mode, which needs the repository.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R6.2, §7. in-toto: a step records its exact materials and products, and verification checks the links against the layout — provenance is a relation between an exact step, exact inputs and exact outputs.
attrs.statement: A transition receipt binds the transitive evidence closure of every settled claim and decision it promotes — witnesses, argument evidence, instrument implementations, incident reproducers, and the relative-import closure of every executable among them — not only the registries and gates the transition itself invoked.

attrs.evidence: True as stated at INV-R6.2 and too weak to be worth stating alone, which is why it is superseded rather than repaired. GPT-5.6 measured the implementation against its own prose twice. attrs.evidence: Both alternatives were tried in argument and refused. INV-R6.2 refused to rewrite the tree so that INV-R6.1 contained no R7 material, because that means deleting a concurrent agent's round and re-authoring it from the migration scripts of the party whose collision caused the problem — a receipt describing a transition no session performed. That refusal was right. What did not follow is that the mixed branch should stay canonical HEAD: those are not the only two options. INV-R8-RECOVERY starts from the INV-R6 commit in an isolated worktree, replays the reviewed content of INV-R6.1, the concurrent INV-R7 and INV-R6.2, and is promoted as a single child of INV-R6 under a revision id no quarantined receipt uses. The damaged branch is preserved unedited on refs/heads/invariant-quarantine. No fabricated intermediate transition is required, and the history says one true thing where it used to say two contradictory ones.
attrs.gap: The replay was performed and reviewed BY THE SAME EVALUATOR that implemented the round — mosaic/objectives.json §exteriority, unsatisfied for a fifth consecutive round. What makes this weaker than a clean history rather than equal to one: `INV-R8-RECOVERY.tree_delta` is derived from bytes and is exact, but WHICH of the mixed branch's changes were intended is a judgement, and the brief carries it in prose. The reviewed-versus-replayed correspondence is checkable only by reading ROUND8_RECOVERY_BRIEF.md against the quarantined artifact.

attrs.statement: A damaged lineage is repaired by ONE new transition from the last verified-good ancestor that replays the reviewed content of the damaged branch under a fresh revision id — not by rewriting the damaged receipts and not by continuing from them.

attrs.evidence: INV-R9 named every hole INV-R9.2 closes, in three separate structured fields, and shipped the claim PROVED beside all three. ARG-INTEGRATION-DIFF-COVERAGE.remaining_trust: “That candidate_count itself is the true size of the delta — it is written by the generator from the pinned artifacts and is NOT recomputed at gate time.” FAC-INTEGRATION-REVIEWED-DIFF.gap: “the file buckets are asserted by the generator rather than checked.” The manifest’s own _comment: “Every count in this file is computed by scripts/gen-manifest” — naming a path that is not in the tree and never was. Each is exactly the premise a later mutation exploited. MEASURED across the ledger: 3 of 19 arguments declare remaining trust in the language of not-checked, all three on PROVED claims; the other two are residuals genuinely outside the artifact’s reach (a computed dynamic import that no witness uses; a domain-extension re-run) and were not exploitable. So the pattern is real and rare, and one of three was load-bearing.
attrs.gap: THE RULE AS STATED IS NOT MECHANISABLE — deciding whether a residual premise is one the conclusion quantifies over is the definitional-subsumption problem again. The DECIDABLE SHADOW, in the sense INV-R7.3 used for non-bypassability, is a phrase test over `remaining_trust` on arguments concluding settled claims, and it is REPORTED by check-claim-ledger rather than gated: a rule that reads as enforced while catching only the phrasings someone thought of is worse than an open claim (H8-SERIALIZABLE-PROMOTION, INV-R8). This is the round’s open question and it is put to the adjudicator rather than answered here.
attrs.prior_art: INV-R8.2 established the special case: SELF-DOUBT IN A COVERING LETTER IS NOT A REFUSAL — a suspect rule flagged in its own handoff and shipped anyway. This generalises it from the covering letter to the ledger’s own structured honesty fields: a `gap` is not a gate.
attrs.review_focus: Is there a form of this rule that binds without becoming a phrase list? The candidate shape is that a coverage argument’s remaining_trust must name only premises OUTSIDE the conclusion’s quantification domain, which needs the domain to be a machine object rather than a sentence.
attrs.statement: A claim may not be PROVED while an argument leg supporting it declares, in `remaining_trust`, that a premise its own conclusion quantifies over is not checked. The honesty fields of this ledger record residual trust; they do not discharge it, and nothing currently stops a disclosure from standing in for a refusal.

attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6's record, adopted as open. The distinction is already PROVED one level down: LED-C9-MEDIATED for the absorbing sink, LED-NARROW for the half that is NOT forbidden (allocating unspent budget remains feasible; only recovering spent value is refused). What is missing is the lift from resources to operations. A source edit is reversible by git; a migration is often only compensatable; publishing a secret is irreversible; training a descendant on an artifact may be harder to revoke than deleting the artifact.
attrs.prior_art: The affine ledger's reversible/irreversible split (in-tree). Externally, reversibility taxonomies for agent actions distinguish instantly reversible, multi-step reversible, and irreversible-without-external-intervention, and note that time sensitivity is a separate axis — cited for the shape of the vocabulary, not for a threshold.
attrs.statement: Every factory operation declares whether its semantic effects are reversible, compensatable or irreversible, and promotion policy holds irreversible effects to a stricter evidence and authority threshold.

attrs.evidence: The round's result, and it is about the factory rather than the product. INV-R6.1 and a concurrent INV-R7 Embodiment round were written into one working tree at the same time, both branching from INV-R6. The R6.1 receipt then claimed ONE parent and ONE operation over a state containing two, and disclosed the ambiguity in prose. That disclosure was honest and insufficient: a transition receipt exists to identify an exact parent, an exact operation and an exact successor, and one that cannot is byte-consistent with a history that did not happen. This is the C10 shape at transition scope — two descriptions of what happened, diverging. The discipline is database serializability applied to recursive self-improvement: read parent P, work against an isolated snapshot of P, verify canonical HEAD is still P before promoting, and on drift abort, rebase, or record an explicit two-parent merge. LOCALLY VALID CONCURRENT IMPROVEMENTS DO NOT AUTOMATICALLY COMPOSE INTO AN HONESTLY IDENTIFIED GLOBAL SUCCESSOR. AT INV-R8-RECOVERY: the counterexample is preserved rather than repaired. INV-R6.1 and INV-R6.2 keep their bytes and are QUARANTINED — never an ancestor of the canonical head — and the canonical head is one recovery_replay whose single parent is the verified INV-R6. Preserving bad history does not require continuing to build on it.
attrs.gap: THE ENFORCEMENT HALF NOW EXISTS AND HAS BEEN USED EXACTLY ONCE. scripts/factory-station.mjs opens an isolated worktree at the canonical head, and promotes with `git update-ref <ref> <new> <old>`, which advances the ref only if it still holds the expected parent OID. INV-R8-RECOVERY is the first round promoted through it. WHAT IS STILL NOT TRUE: the station cannot bind a session that never calls it. The canonical state is the REF, not the shared directory, and a session writing the directory is not promoting anything — but it is also not refused. Measured during this round: at 17:17 on 2026-08-24 a third concurrent session rewrote mosaic/embodiment.json in the shared tree with no transition at all, and the head receipt's digest for that path stopped reproducing. `factory-station.mjs verify --worktree` reports such a divergence in one line; it does not prevent it. The claim also remains DECLARED because one promotion is not "every promoted round".

attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6's record, adopted as open, and the reason it matters is that it removes a false prerequisite: a factory does not have to prove an experimental component correct before the component may ever be useful. It has to contain it. The prior art is mature and was verified this round rather than accepted on citation.
attrs.gap: Adopted as a station-contract PATTERN (assurance_mode: simplex | sandbox | canary | shadow | none), explicitly NOT as a tenth artifact.
attrs.prior_art: The Simplex architecture (an unverified high-performance controller under a decision module with a trusted fallback). Phan, Yang, Clark, Grosu, Schierman, Smolka & Stoller, 'A Component-Based Simplex Architecture for High-Assurance Cyber-Physical Systems' (arXiv 1704.04759, 2017) integrates assume-guarantee reasoning with Simplex and composes instances in nested, serial and parallel arrangements — verified 2026-08-24, and the closest neighbour to the Contract Registry this Mosaic is building.
attrs.statement: A station running an unverified or self-modifying candidate declares an assurance envelope, a monitor, a fallback and a switching condition, and its promotion evidence records whether the candidate ever crossed the envelope.

attrs.evidence: The mapping is measured derivable (FAC-ID-WALK-R83) and the reader protocol that makes the derivation authoritative is declared (FAC-PUBLICATION-IDENTITY). What is NOT done is the consequence: the tags are still created by the publication transaction and still carry retention duty for the draft and quarantine heads, which are NOT on the receipt chain and therefore NOT reconstructible from it. Pruning canonical tags before naming who owns retention of the unreconstructible ones would delete the only handle on INV-R8.1's five superseded drafts and on the quarantine head.
attrs.gap: OPEN ON PURPOSE AND THE REASON IS THE INTERESTING PART. Deriving the tag would remove a ref from the publication transaction, and FAC-PUBLICATION-ATOMIC was written because publishing across two refs had a window. Removing the second ref satisfies that claim trivially rather than by mechanism — which is a better design and a worse test, because the property would stop being exercised. Doing both in one round would mean shipping a repair to a mechanism while removing the mechanism. Second: retention ownership is unassigned. Third: the scope is lightweight tags only.
