attrs.statement: Canonical lightweight revision tags are a derived navigation and retention index, not a second identity authority. Nothing may establish revision identity by reading a tag, and no tag may be pruned until an explicit retention owner is declared.

attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6's best addition, and neither Mosaic proposal had made the join object first class: without it, Objective, Contract, Evidence, Operation and Lineage records can each be individually valid while referring to different versions. Implemented for one transition — mosaic/receipts/INV-R5.json binds R4.1 to R5 — and the gate verifies the head receipt's digests against the files they name. ONE CORRECTION TO GPT'S FRAMING, and it is the C10 incident at factory scale: a receipt WRITTEN AFTER the gate ran is a log, not a gate, and two representations of one decision drift. The receipt's `decision` field must be the output of the same predicate the promotion consults, or the pair is exactly `feasible` disagreeing with `charge`. This round does not close that: R5's receipt is written after its gates ran, and says so in its own `honesty` field.
attrs.prior_art: in-toto link metadata (authorized functionary, command, materials, products, verified against a layout) is the shape. Tan, Singer & Anagnostopoulos, 'Attesting LLM Pipelines: Enforcing Verifiable Training and Release Claims' (LLMSC 2026 workshop, arXiv 2603.28988) proposes an attestation-aware PROMOTION GATE with allow/quarantine/block over claim bundles — the closest published relative, and a workshop position paper rather than a mature standard. SLSA v1.2 (approved 24 Nov 2025) supplies Build and Source track attestations and states the separation this record depends on: it records evidence, and policy decides what is acceptable.
attrs.review_focus: The receipt is descriptive this round, not decisive. Attack the gap between 'the receipt records what the gates decided' and 'the gate decides by reading the receipt' — the second is the version that cannot drift, and it is not built.
attrs.statement: Every attempted promotion emits one immutable receipt binding the exact predecessor state, candidate, operation, contract set, invariant delta, objective portfolio, evidence set, evaluator versions, authority and decision. A promotion whose references do not resolve to one coherent versioned state is invalid.

attrs.evidence: INV-R6.2 reported "all 15 digest(s) reproduce" against the clean INV-R6 bundle and concluded that INV-R6 is BYTE-RECOVERABLE from its own receipt. What was established is that the 15 paths INV-R6's receipt happened to digest match the supplied snapshot — and the reason INV-R6.2 exists is that R6-era receipt scope was INCOMPLETE. Fifteen matching files cannot identify a fifty-file tree; the snapshot is a recovery source and the receipt is not yet an identity. Every receipt from INV-R8-RECOVERY on carries `candidate.tree_manifest_sha256`, a sha256 over `sha  path` for every path in the tree, and `parent.commit_oid` where a repository exists. --reconstruct now says which of the two claims it is making instead of printing the stronger sentence over the weaker fact.
attrs.gap: The manifest necessarily EXCLUDES the head receipt itself — a receipt cannot carry the digest of a tree that contains it — and for the same reason `candidate.commit_oid` is absent from the receipt and recorded as a git tag instead. Both exclusions are stated in the receipt rather than worked around. The tree-manifest form is only as good as the path set fed to it, which is FAC-RECEIPT-EVIDENCE-CLOSED's problem; the commit form does not have that weakness and is why the receipt carries both.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R6.2, §6. SLSA v1.2 provenance: an artifact is traced to exact resolved dependencies — a specific commit rather than a floating repository reference.
attrs.statement: A transition identifies its parent and its candidate by WHOLE-TREE identity — a commit OID, or a deterministic manifest digest over every path in the tree — not by the list of files a receipt chose to digest.

assumptions: D finite
Γ a finite set of finitary relations on D
attrs.evidence: Derived from standard finite-CSP algebra: every finite structure has a core (Hell–Nešetřil 1992); endomorphisms preserve pp-definable relations; the canonical conjunctive query at an element of a finite core pp-defines its automorphism orbit. (⇐) transitivity makes every non-empty pp-definable unary relation contain the whole core. (⇒) two orbits give two disjoint non-empty pp-definable unary relations. Checked on nine languages against the symmetry certificate and the bounded search, with no disagreement on any conclusive result.
attrs.prior_art: Ingredients standard — Hell–Nešetřil 1992 (cores); Bodirsky, Graph Homomorphisms and Universal Algebra Prop. 5.10 (pp-definable orbits); Jeavons–Cohen–Gyssens 1997 (Inv–Pol). NOVELTY OF THE EQUIVALENCE IS NOT CLAIMED and no exact prior-art search has been done: publish it as "the constraint template has a transitive core", derived here, not as a named classical theorem.
attrs.review_focus: The equivalence is short and its ingredients are textbook, which is exactly the profile of a result someone has already published. FED-1PA-NAME is the search, and it is still open.
attrs.statement: Γ has the one-variable gluing property (working-1PA) if and only if the automorphism group of the core of (D; Γ) acts transitively on the core.

assumptions: Cited, not re-derived, and NOT implemented.
attrs.evidence: P(Γ) is the set of non-empty pp-definable unary relations; by the Inv–Pol Galois connection those are exactly the unary relations preserved by all polymorphisms of Γ, and bounded arity suffices over a finite domain.

source_assumptions: Gamma a finite set of finitary relations

attrs.gap: What IS implemented is a bounded search for a 1PA VIOLATION (conclusive when it hits) and a symmetry certificate (conclusive when it applies). A miss from the bounded search is NOT a proof of 1PA and the code says so. Do not report '1PA holds' on the strength of it.
attrs.note: ASSUMPTION_REFS ADDED AT R6, not by review but by the canonical removal test: deleting every argument-assumption edge in the tree cost zero refusals, which meant nothing checked that an argument's hypotheses reached its conclusion. ARG-FED-1PA-DEC-CITATION had always rested on ASM-D-FINITE and ASM-GAMMA-FINITE and this record had always read as unconditional.
attrs.prior_art: Geiger 1968; Bodnarchuk–Kalužnin–Kotov–Romov 1969; Jeavons–Cohen–Gyssens 1997.
attrs.statement: 1PA is a decidable property of a finite constraint language.

assumptions: |D|^|D| endomorphism enumeration is affordable — the implementation refuses above a declared bound rather than hanging
attrs.evidence: decide1PA enumerates End(A), takes a minimum-image endomorphism f, builds the genuine retraction r = p⁻¹∘f (p = f restricted to the image, a bijection because minimality forces f(B) = B), and tests transitivity of Aut(B) over permutations of B. The retraction is checked to be idempotent, identity on the core, and an endomorphism. refute1PA builds the two-site canonical-query federation; on every failing language it has both sites satisfiable, exactly one shared variable, κ_splitBerge = 0, and an unsatisfiable union.
attrs.prior_art: The procedure follows from FED-1PA-DEC being KNOWN; what is claimed here is that it runs and agrees. REPEATED SQUARING IS NOT A CORE RETRACTION — iterating f^(2^k) never reaches an idempotent for a permutation of order 3 — and the round-3 research implementation returned a map under that name that was not one. GPT-5.6, round-3 audit.
attrs.statement: The exact decision procedure for the transitive-core property is implemented here and is conclusive in both directions, returning a running refutation when the property fails.

attrs.evidence: None. The sharp question is whether the language can pp-define TWO DISJOINT non-empty unary projections — equivalently, whether ⋂U_Γ is empty (FED-1PA-HELLY). ROUND 3 sharpened what has to be specified before this can be decided at all: sorts, a domain model per sort, relation symbols with sorted scopes, which literals/constants are admitted as atoms, and which schema-level universal constraints (keys, mandatory participation, uniqueness) lie OUTSIDE the instance-CSP model. The multi-sorted theorem is available — the property holds at separator sort σ iff Aut(core) is transitive on the σ-part — but the CORE IS GLOBAL to the multi-sorted structure and is not obtained by solving each sort independently. Indicative reading of representative fragments: identity sorts with =/≠ pass; a value sort passes until it carries two literals, and then fails. That makes 36b, not 36a, the likely route for real value sorts.
attrs.gap: This is the load-bearing open question under cell 36 and the reason its status is `conditional` rather than `proved`.
attrs.review_focus: No FGAP language exists in a form precise enough to decide this. Representative Neo4j/GQL-like fragments are examples, not the user's language, and classifying them settles nothing about FGAP.
attrs.statement: The constraint languages a real federated property graph would carry have 1PA.
attrs.supersedes: Round 2 asserted that 'if any federated relation can pin a variable to a value, 1PA fails outright'. THAT IS FALSE, and it was the sentence the practical question was built on. Over D = {0,1} a language whose only pin is x = 0 realizes projections {0} and {0,1}, which intersect — so it pins a value AND has 1PA. Failure needs two DISJOINT projections, e.g. pp-defining both {0} and {1}. Both cases are now checked in §4. Correction from GPT-5.6's round-2 audit.

assumptions: Finite domain. The executable corroboration runs over a BOUNDED subfamily of U_Γ (instances of ≤3 constraints, ≤2 auxiliary variables), so it corroborates the equivalence rather than deciding 1PA for a language.
attrs.evidence: (⟸) a common element makes every pair intersect. (⟹) under 1PA, U_Γ is closed under non-empty intersection: given U, V realized by I₁, I₂, rename auxiliary variables apart and identify only x; the union is satisfiable by 1PA and its projection at x is exactly U ∩ V. D is finite, so U_Γ is finite, so ⋂U_Γ is a finite intersection of members and is itself a member — hence non-empty. ∎ Checked on six languages including the two that fail: pairwise-intersecting ⟺ a common element exists, 0 mismatches, and closure under intersection holds wherever 1PA does. ROUND 3: this is a corollary of the transitive-core theorem and NOT a prior-art search key. Closure of U_Γ under intersection holds for every Γ — pp-definable relations are closed under conjunction — so the "Helly" content is a fact about pp-definability, not a property of the language. It remains true and remains a useful reformulation; it is just not the thing to look up.
attrs.gap: This form is simpler than the pairwise one and may yield both a decision procedure and the established name. Contributed by GPT-5.6 in the round-2 audit.
attrs.prior_art: NOT SEARCHED, and this is the highest-value prior-art target in the round. 'Every pair intersects ⟹ the whole family intersects' is a HELLY property; Helly properties of constraint languages, unary pp-definable relations under Inv–Pol, and variable-elimination properties are the neighbourhoods to search. Novelty is not claimed.
attrs.statement: Γ has 1PA ⟺ the intersection of ALL non-empty unary pp-definable projections of Γ is non-empty — i.e. some single domain value belongs to every member of U_Γ = { π_x(sol I) : I a satisfiable Γ-instance }.

assumptions: D finite
the core of (D; Γ) is automorphism-transitive
attrs.evidence: ⋂U_Γ is pp-definable, contains B, and is End-invariant, so it contains every h(B); conversely it is contained in the member End(A)·b. Checked by requiring every bounded realized projection to contain the computed hull, on every language of the §4b table where the property holds.
attrs.prior_art: Corollary of FED-1PA-CORE.
attrs.statement: When Γ has a transitive core B, the intersection of all non-empty unary pp-definable relations of Γ equals End(A)·b for any b in B — the endomorphic hull of the core.

attrs.evidence: Successor on a 6-path over |D| = 6 fails the property — its core is all of D with six singleton orbits — and find1PAViolation reports null at its default bounds. The witness appears only at maxAux 3. The bounded search remains a sound FALSIFIER: a hit exhibits its witness. It was never a decision procedure and this is the construction that says so. TIMELESS because the bounds are named in the statement: raising the defaults does not make a miss AT THESE BOUNDS conclusive, it produces a different proposition. R4.1 REMOVED AN OVERREACH HERE. R3.1 appended "FED-WITNESS-BOUND makes the minimum grow with Σ|R^A|, so no fixed bound is ever conclusive" — which is an upper bound on the minimum used as a lower one, and is false (FED-MIN-GROWS). The universal statement it was reaching for is now open as FED-1PA-NO-FIXED-BOUND, unsupported.
attrs.prior_art: Fable 5, round-3 research pass.
attrs.statement: A MISS from find1PAViolation at its default bounds (maxCon 3, maxAux 2) is evidence that Γ has the gluing property.

attrs.evidence: Round 3 eliminated three candidates without finding the answer. "1-point amalgamation" collides with the Fraïssé-theoretic one-point amalgamation property and is retired as a public name. "Patchwork" (Lutz–Miličić; Dabrowski et al. AAAI 2021) is a DIFFERENT property — it quantifies over complete satisfiable JEPD networks agreeing on their whole overlap, hypotheses the general finite-template condition does not carry — though the exact relationship in that restricted setting is not settled, and calling the two incomparable outright would overstate it. The common-intersection form is NOT the search key it was proposed as: the closure step needs no hypothesis on Γ at all, so the "Helly property" there is a triviality of pp-closure rather than a property of the language. The nearest classical analogue found is Huang 2012's canonical-solution characterization of patchwork, of which the transitive core is the single-variable case. Until an exact citation exists, publish the descriptive phrase "the constraint template has a transitive core" and claim no name.
attrs.gap: Do not publish `1PA` as settled terminology. Establishing the exact existing name — best attacked via the FED-1PA-HELLY common-intersection form — is the first objective of the next research pass.
attrs.prior_art: Fraïssé amalgamation (collision) · Dabrowski–Jonsson–Ordyniak–Osipov AAAI 2021 (patchwork) · Huang 2012 (canonical solutions) · Bodirsky, Graph Homomorphisms and Universal Algebra (cores, pp-definable orbits). ROUND-4 AUDIT ADDED A UNIVERSAL-ALGEBRA SEARCH FORMULATION, which is a better key than the two already eliminated: for a finite core, transitivity of Aut is equivalent to the polymorphism algebra having NO PROPER NON-EMPTY SUBUNIVERSES. (⟸) each automorphism orbit of a finite core is pp-definable and hence a unary subuniverse, so two orbits give a proper one. (⟹) transitivity leaves no proper invariant subset. Literature on finite transitive cores uses the "no proper subalgebras" consequence explicitly, so that phrase — not "canonical value" and not pp-definable unary relations — is where to search next.
attrs.review_focus: An exact prior-art search for the EQUIVALENCE ITSELF has still not been done. Two search framings are now eliminated and a third (no proper subuniverses) is untried. If it is already published, FED-1PA-CORE should be KNOWN and not PROVED.
attrs.statement: '1-point amalgamation' is the correct name for this property.

attrs.evidence: NOT PROVED, and R3.1 asserted it. It is plausible — probably true — and the only argument offered for it was invalid: FED-WITNESS-BOUND bounds the canonical construction from above and says nothing about how small a refutation can be, which FED-MIN-GROWS makes concrete. Establishing it needs a LOWER-bound family: languages whose MINIMUM refutation size diverges. Note the shape of what is required — not a language with a large canonical query, which is easy, but one where no small refutation exists at all, which is the hard direction and the reason this is a research question rather than a measurement.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6, round-5 audit, which separated this from the default-bounds fact.
attrs.review_focus: This is the load-bearing proposition behind "a bounded search can never decide the property", and nothing here establishes it. Any future claim that a bounded search is inconclusive IN GENERAL must cite this record, and this record is open.
attrs.statement: For every fixed search bound B there is a finite Γ that fails the gluing property but whose every refutation exceeds B.

attrs.evidence: Solution sets of Γ-instances are H-invariant. If I₁, I₂ share only x with solutions α₁, α₂, pick h with h(α₁(x)) = α₂(x); then h∘α₁ ∪ α₂ solves the union. eq/neq is Sym(D)-invariant at every |D|.
attrs.prior_art: Elementary. The polymorphism framing is Jeavons–Cohen–Gyssens 1997.
attrs.statement: If a transitive subgroup of Sym(D) preserves every relation of Γ, then Γ has 1-point amalgamation. (Lemma 3.)

attrs.evidence: Γ = {R} with R = {(0,1),(1,0),(2,1),(1,2)} over |D| = 3. Aut(D; R) fixes 1 (the only degree-2 element) so it is not transitive and the certificate fails, but the retraction 2 ↦ 0 gives the core {0,1} on which Aut acts transitively — so the property HOLDS. Value symmetry is strictly stronger than the real condition, which is what makes FED-1PA-SYM a certificate rather than a characterization.
attrs.prior_art: Fable 5, round-3 research pass.
attrs.statement: Value symmetry — a transitive subgroup of Sym(D) preserving every relation of Γ — is NECESSARY for the gluing property.

attrs.evidence: (⟸) a split cycle is 2-connected, hence contained in one block, which then carries ≥2 sites. (⟹) any two edges of a block lie on a common cycle, so a block with two sites yields a split cycle. Checked against brute-force enumeration of every simple cycle (including 2-cycles from parallel edges) on 117,648 federations: 0 mismatches.
attrs.prior_art: Block decomposition: Whitney 1932; Diestel Graph Theory §3.1.
attrs.statement: κₛ(G, site) := Σ over blocks B of max(0, |sites(B)| − 1) is zero exactly when no cycle of the carrier is split across sites.

attrs.evidence: Matroid components are the classes of "lie on a common circuit" (Oxley §4.1); for the cycle matroid of a loopless graph the circuits are the cycles and the components are the block edge sets; a separator is a union of components (§4.2) and a partition into separators is a direct-sum decomposition. Verified against κₛ on 117,648 binary federations and on 4,096 n-ary federations, zero mismatches on all three equivalences. This unifies the carriers: for binary constraints the incidence graph is the subdivision of the constraint multigraph, so ONE carrier now covers every arity and the two-carrier machinery retires.
attrs.prior_art: Oxley, Matroid Theory §4.1–4.2 (components, separators, direct sums) — a KNOWN TRANSLATION of a standard matroid fact, not a new theorem. Whitney 1932 for blocks.
attrs.statement: κₛ = 0 if and only if every site's incidence-edge set is a separator of the cycle matroid of the incidence graph — equivalently the site colouring is constant on every matroid component, equivalently the matroid is the direct sum of its site restrictions.

assumptions: "canonical" is not formalized anywhere in this work, which is why this is DECLARED and not open to refutation as stated
attrs.evidence: NOT DERIVED, and round 3 did not refute it either. Five natural magnitudes — impure-component count; Σ max(0, |sites(B)| − 1); minimum recolourings; minimum carrier deletions to purify; and the partition-lattice gap |sites| − #components of the site-conflict graph (the minimum number of site merges, and the only one with a matroid meaning) — are pairwise distinct, all ten pairs separated by explicit federations. That shows the theorem FIXES no magnitude; it does not show none is canonical, because "canonical" has not been defined. The research pass filed this as "canonical magnitude REFUTED"; that is a polarity and formalization error and is not adopted. Sharper evidence against all five: the zero set agrees between the binary constraint multigraph and its incidence-graph subdivision while the magnitudes do not — minimum recolouring reads 2 on a three-site triangle and 4 on its subdivision. THE CLASS IS NAMED DELIBERATELY: what is proved is invariance under THAT ONE normalization, not under some unspecified family of carrier transformations, and "carrier-invariant" should not be published as a general phrase until such a class is defined.
attrs.review_focus: A declared index is the kind of thing that gets cited as if it were derived. If a magnitude is wanted, the first job is to say what "canonical" would mean — invariance under which operations? — and the carrier-invariance failure is the sharpest available test.
attrs.statement: The MAGNITUDE of κₛ is a canonical invariant.

attrs.evidence: Six explicit federations separate all ten pairs. The round-3 research witness printed "magnitudes shown pairwise distinct" while its code compared six hand-listed pairs out of ten, and on its five examples the impure-component count and the minimum-purifying-deletion count are NEVER different. GPT-5.6 caught it and proposed the missing witness: K₄ with one site on a perfect matching has ONE impure component (K₄ is 2-connected, so one block) and needs TWO deletions, because K₄ minus any single edge is still 2-connected and still mixed. That witness is added and all ten pairs are now compared programmatically rather than listed.
attrs.prior_art: Fable 5 (the five magnitudes) · GPT-5.6 (the K₄ separator and the incomplete-pair-list finding).
attrs.statement: The five candidate κₛ magnitudes are pairwise distinct: for each of the ten unordered pairs there is a federation on which they differ.

attrs.evidence: b₁ cannot see the site colouring, and the colouring is the whole content. A single site holding a triangle has b₁ = 1 and NO split cycle, so b₁ reports an obstruction the federation theorem says is absent. b₁ = 0 and κₛ = 0 disagree on 1,440 of the 15,624 four-variable federations.
attrs.prior_art: Proposed by Fable 5 as patch B3; refuted by GPT-5.6 in audit and by the witness here.
attrs.statement: Ordinary undirected cycle rank b₁ = |E| − |V| + c is the right replacement for κ as cell 36's carrier.

attrs.evidence: κ is defined on DIRECTED graphs via the largest SCC. Constraint edges are symmetric, so every orientation is arbitrary. CE-D: sites {a≠b, b≠d} and {a=c, c≠d}, oriented a→b, a→c, b→d, c→d — all SCCs trivial, κ = 0, and fidelity fails on the undirected split 4-cycle underneath.
attrs.statement: κ as defined in cell 01 carries the federation obstruction of cell 36.
attrs.supersedes: INV-R1 §2 and §3, which asserted '#36's obstruction is cyclicity, which is what #01 κ already measures' and rested the I ↔ X cross-family link on it.

attrs.evidence: Take the pins p₀, p₁ over |D| = 2 — whose refutation p₀(x) | p₁(x) is TWO constraints — and adjoin an irrelevant full k-ary relation. Every map preserves a full relation, so End(A) and the core are unchanged and the language still fails the property; but Σ|R^A| gains 2^k. Measured against the shipped kernel: k=1 gives Σ = 4 and a canonical construction of 8; k=4 gives 18 and 36; k=8 gives 258 and 516 — and at every k the two-constraint witness is still there, with both sites satisfiable, κ_splitBerge = 0 and an unsatisfiable union. AN UPPER BOUND ON THE MINIMUM BOUNDS NOTHING FROM BELOW. This record exists because R3.1 asserted the proposition above while citing FED-WITNESS-BOUND, which establishes the opposite direction; the family is pinned rather than the sentence merely deleted.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6, round-5 audit, which supplied the family and the measurements.
attrs.statement: The minimum refutation size for a language failing the gluing property grows with Σ_{R∈Γ}|R^A|.

assumptions: Cited, not implemented here.
attrs.evidence: BFMY 1983, both directions. Note this rehabilitates INV-R1's refuted 'nerve' conjecture in corrected form: the refutation used the nerve GRAPH, in which a star of sites is a cyclic K₃; the nerve HYPERGRAPH of a star is α-acyclic. The intuition was right and the carrier was wrong.

local_bindings.scheme: the union hypergraph of the federation

attrs.gap: The two certificates give incomparable sufficient conditions. Cell 36 must state which one a given federation actually provides; it currently describes only the local-satisfiability route.
attrs.prior_art: Beeri–Fagin–Maier–Yannakakis 1983.
attrs.statement: If sites certify PAIRWISE CONSISTENCY of their solution projections rather than only local satisfiability, the carrier is α-acyclicity of the SITE hypergraph.

attrs.evidence: Four constructions. CE-A kills it on a TREE (site 1 pins v=0, site 2 pins v=1; the carrier is the path a–v–b, so there is no cycle to split) — cyclicity is therefore not the obstruction at all for a general language. CE-B does it at |D|=2 with every relation having full projections, refuting the natural 'arc-consistent language' repair. CE-C repeats the shape at |D|=3 with Z₃ sums.
attrs.finding: REFUTED. The implication fails for general finite constraint languages; the counterexample is exhibited by the gate.
attrs.prior_art: Discovered by Fable 5, 2026-08-23. Not previously stated in this tree.
attrs.statement: For general finite constraint languages, no cycle of the union carrier being split across sites ⟹ fidelity.
attrs.supersedes: INV-R1's evidence line '4 domains, 240k trials, 0 counterexamples', which was evidence for nothing beyond eq/neq: every domain sampled the same value-symmetric language, for which the lemma is a short theorem. The sweep was measuring a theorem, not probing a conjecture.

assumptions: Γ has 1-point amalgamation (1PA): any two satisfiable Γ-instances sharing exactly one variable have a satisfiable union.
attrs.evidence: Block–cut induction. No split cycle ⟺ every block with ≥2 edges is monochromatic (Whitney: any two edges of a 2-connected graph lie on a common cycle), so each block is a sub-multiset of one satisfiable site. Blocks and cut vertices form a TREE; a leaf block meets the rest in exactly one variable; 1PA glues. Corroborated exhaustively: 0 violations over every no-split-cycle federation in a complete 4-variable enumeration at |D|=2 and |D|=3.
attrs.prior_art: PROVED HERE by block–cut induction. Beeri–Fagin–Maier–Yannakakis 1983 is the neighbouring classical result (pairwise ⟹ global consistency on α-acyclic schemes) and the block hypergraph is α-acyclic, but BFMY's pairwise consistency is STRICTLY STRONGER than 1PA's intersecting-projections condition, so this is not a restatement of it. Novelty is NOT claimed — an exact prior-art search has not been done. Explicitly NOT Freuder 1982, which assumes arc consistency of the whole network; CE-A satisfies this cell's antecedent and violates Freuder's.
attrs.statement: If Γ has 1-point amalgamation and no cycle of the union carrier is split across sites, then fidelity holds.

attrs.evidence: (⇐) is FED-Q1-STAR. (⇒) is a construction, and it runs: given two satisfiable instances meeting at one variable with disjoint projections there, make each its own site. They meet at a cut vertex, so no cycle is split; both sites are satisfiable; the union is not. The check finds such a pair for {OR, NAND} at |D|=2 and verifies all four properties of the resulting federation.
attrs.prior_art: As FED-Q1-STAR. Labelled proved-here; not attributed to BFMY.
attrs.statement: Split-cycle sufficiency holds for EVERY Γ-federation if and only if Γ has 1-point amalgamation.

assumptions: the existence of graphs with girth > s and chromatic number > k is Erdős 1959, cited and NOT re-derived here
the executable instance is s = 3, k = 3 only; larger s rests on the citation
attrs.evidence: Take G with girth > s and χ(G) > k. All-≠ on G with one site per edge: every site satisfiable, the union not k-colourable, fidelity fails. Any sub-federation of ≤ s constraints has ≤ s edges and girth > s, so it is a forest, 2-colourable, and has fidelity — soundness fails. Instantiated executably with the Grötzsch graph (11 vertices, 20 edges, girth 4, χ = 4): all 1,140 three-constraint sub-federations have fidelity while the whole does not. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE POINT — for k ≥ 3 a fidelity failure can be irreducibly GLOBAL, carried by no bounded piece of the federation.

evidence_qualifiers.scope: The executable instance is s = 3, k = 3 only; larger s rests on ASM-ERDOS-GIRTH and ARG-FED-Q2-BOUNDED-CITATION.

attrs.prior_art: Erdős, Graph theory and probability, Canad. J. Math 11 (1959). NOT a first-order or Hanf-locality statement: that needs matching neighbourhood-type counts and is a separate theorem nothing here attempts.
attrs.review_focus: The quantifier class is bounded-size SUB-FEDERATIONS. A criterion allowed to inspect several pieces jointly, or to compute a global aggregate, is untouched by this — and that is a strictly larger and more interesting class.
attrs.statement: For every k ≥ 3 and every fixed size bound s, no test of the form "∃ a sub-federation of at most s constraints satisfying T" is both sound and complete for fidelity failure.

assumptions: the language is eq/neq
every site is locally satisfiable — WITHOUT this the ⟸ direction is false
attrs.evidence: Harary 1953: a signed graph is balanced iff every cycle carries an even number of negative edges, iff its vertices 2-colour. Exhaustive over 117,648 federations: 0 mismatches. The literal conjecture, stated without the antecedent, fails on 15,744 of them — an unbalanced split cycle sitting beside a locally unsatisfiable site makes fidelity vacuously true.
attrs.prior_art: Harary 1953 (balance).
attrs.statement: At |D| = 2 over eq/neq, under the antecedent that every site is satisfiable, fidelity fails if and only if some split cycle is unbalanced in Harary's signed-graph sense (an odd number of ≠ edges).

assumptions: The quantifier class is exactly as defined: P sees the cycle's own labels and site tags and nothing else. A criterion permitted to inspect the rest of the federation, or several cycles jointly, is NOT covered and is a different question.
attrs.evidence: Suppose P is sound and complete. Let F be K₄ all-≠ in three matchings; ¬fidelity(F), so by completeness some cycle C of F satisfies P. Let F' be the federation whose constraints are exactly C's edges with the same relations and site tags. C is a cycle of F', so FAIL_P(F') holds. But F' is a single ≠-cycle: 3-colourable, with every site a sub-multiset of a matching, so fidelity(F') HOLDS — contradicting soundness. ∎ The load-bearing step is checked: all 7 of K₄'s simple cycles keep fidelity when extracted. The |D|=2 contrast is checked too — an unbalanced split cycle STILL fails fidelity when extracted, which is exactly why 'split and unbalanced' is a valid cycle-local criterion there.
attrs.prior_art: Not searched. The statement is elementary once the quantifier class is fixed; the point of fixing it is that the previous informal version could not be attacked.
attrs.review_focus: Proved ONLY for the quantifier class it names. A criterion permitted to inspect several cycles jointly, or the rest of the federation, is untouched — and that is a strictly larger and more interesting class.
attrs.statement: Define a CYCLE-LOCAL CRITERION as a predicate P on (labels(C), sites(C)) — the relations and site tags along a cycle, in order, and nothing else about the federation containing it — inducing the test FAIL_P(F) := ∃ a cycle C of F with P(labels(C), sites(C)). Then at |D| = 3 over {=, ≠} there is NO cycle-local criterion P that is both sound and complete, i.e. satisfies FAIL_P(F) ⟺ ¬fidelity(F) for every federation F.
attrs.superseded_by: FED-Q2-DK-LOCALITY (all k ≥ 3) and FED-Q2-BOUNDED-LOCALITY (all bounded sizes s)

attrs.evidence: χ(K₄) = 4 > 3, so the union has no model. Each site is a perfect matching and trivially satisfiable. Each of the 7 simple cycles is a 3- or 4-cycle of disequalities, and every cycle of ≠ is 2- or 3-colourable. All three facts are computed, not asserted.
attrs.prior_art: The colouring reduction is standard; Erdős 1959 (high girth, high chromatic number) generalizes the construction to arbitrarily large girth.
attrs.statement: At |D| = 3 over {=, ≠}, a fidelity failure need not have any individually unsatisfiable cycle: K₄ with all-≠ edges split into three perfect matchings has every site satisfiable, every simple cycle satisfiable, and no 3-colouring.
attrs.supersedes: The record FED-Q2-D3, which stated the negative proposition 'no cycle-local predicate can characterize fidelity failure' and then marked it REFUTED while citing evidence FOR it. The polarity was backwards and 'cycle-local' was never defined. Split into this witness and FED-Q2-D3-LOCALITY.

assumptions: "cycle-local criterion" as defined in FED-Q2-D3-LOCALITY — a predicate on a cycle's own labels and site tags and nothing else
attrs.evidence: K_{k+1} of all-≠ with one site per edge: every site is a single constraint and so satisfiable, χ(K_{k+1}) = k+1 > k so the union is not, and fidelity fails. Completeness forces P on some cycle; every simple cycle of a complete graph is 2- or 3-colourable and so k-colourable, hence has fidelity when extracted with its own labels and sites, and soundness fails. Executed at k = 3, 4, 5 — 7, 37 and 197 simple cycles respectively, every one keeping fidelity under extraction.
attrs.prior_art: Generalizes the k = 3 case (FED-Q2-D3-LOCALITY) by the same argument.
attrs.statement: For EVERY k ≥ 3, over {=, ≠} on |D| = k, no cycle-local criterion is both sound and complete for fidelity failure.

attrs.evidence: H = {a,b,c},{a,b} with site 1 holding the Sym(D)-invariant ternary 'a = b' and site 2 holding a ≠ b. GYO reduces it (α-acyclic); every sub-hypergraph is α-acyclic (β-acyclic); two edges cannot form a γ-cycle. It is Berge-cyclic, both sites are satisfiable, and the union is not. Sampling agrees: α-acyclic unions violate fidelity thousands of times per run.
attrs.prior_art: Fagin 1983 states the mechanism — two hyperedges sharing ≥2 vertices are already Berge-cyclic, which is exactly why database theory weakened the notion. For a local-satisfiability certificate that weakening is unaffordable.
attrs.statement: α-, β- and γ-acyclicity of the union hypergraph are sufficient carriers for the local-satisfiability certificate.

assumptions: Γ has a transitive core (FED-1PA-CORE) — the hypothesis is load-bearing: the {OR, NAND} control violates the conclusion on the same carrier shape
CONSTRAINTS ARE HYPEREDGE INSTANCES, not scopes — see FED-Q3-INSTANCE
attrs.evidence: Proof: no split Berge cycle ⟺ every block of I(H) is site-monochromatic (any two constraint-nodes of a 2-connected block share a cycle); super-blocks (blocks merged across shared constraint-nodes) are then monochromatic and form a tree whose adjacent members share exactly one variable; a leaf glues by the language hypothesis; induct. CORROBORATION IS NOW EXHAUSTIVE, NOT SAMPLED — the previous 20,000-draw sweep is gone. Four complete small spaces over three languages whose hypothesis is CHECKED rather than labelled (Sym(3)-invariant; {U₀, ≤, =} with a singleton core and a genuine unary relation; {≠∘f, R∘R} with a transitive core and no value symmetry), each federation checked three ways — κ_splitBerge against brute-force incidence-cycle enumeration, super-blocks against an independent subset enumeration of hypergraph vertex-articulation blocks, and the theorem against a full satisfiability solve. Zero mismatches, zero violations. The {OR, NAND} control produces violations on the same carrier shape, so a zero there would mean the hypothesis was doing nothing.
attrs.prior_art: Berge cycles: Fagin 1983.
attrs.review_focus: Sufficiency is proved and NECESSITY at arity > 2 is untouched (FED-Q3-NEC). The exhaustive spaces are small: they cannot express a witness needing more than two constraints per site, which is exactly how FED-Q3-HYP-S4 hid.
attrs.statement: For constraints of arbitrary arity over a language with 1PA, if no BERGE cycle of the union hypergraph is split across sites then fidelity holds.

attrs.evidence: Adding NAE₃ destroys the retraction 2 ↦ 0 — it sends the NAE tuple (2,2,0) to (0,0,0) — so End(A) collapses from 6 maps to 2, the core becomes all of D, and Aut has two orbits: {0,2} and {1}, because 1 is the only degree-2 element of R. The property FAILS, and the canonical-query refutation runs: 56 constraints, two sites, both satisfiable, κ_splitBerge = 0, union unsatisfiable. THIS MATTERS BECAUSE IT WAS A LABEL, NOT A CHECK. The round-3 research pass ran an exhaustive space of 287,496 federations over this language under the heading "transitive core, NOT value-symmetric" and reported zero violations of the theorem. The antecedent was never satisfied, so that space corroborated nothing about the theorem — and the counterexample was missed for the most ordinary reason: 56 constraints do not fit in a pool of ≤2 constraints per site over four variables. EXHAUSTION OVER A SPACE TOO SMALL TO HOLD THE WITNESS IS EXACTLY AS BLIND AS A SAMPLE, and it reads as stronger. Every space in §5 now decides its hypothesis before entering.
attrs.prior_art: Found by this implementation round while porting the research pass's spaces. It is round 1's lesson (240,000 trials over one language is one trial) recurring one level down.
attrs.review_focus: The replacement language has a CHECKED hypothesis, and its space has the same size limit that hid the original problem. FED-WITNESS-BOUND says how large a space would need to be to contain a CANONICAL witness — an upper bound, which is the direction this needs. It does not say a smaller witness cannot exist below that, and for corroboration that is the direction that would matter.
attrs.statement: The language {≠∘f, NAE₃} over |D| = 3 has a transitive core.

attrs.evidence: EQ₃(a,b,q) at site 0 and NAE₃(a,b,q) at site 1. In the instance model the two constraint-nodes form a split Berge 2-cycle, κ_splitBerge = 1, and the theorem is correctly silent — fidelity does fail. Merging the identical scopes gives ONE hyperedge, no Berge cycle at all, κ_splitBerge = 0, and the theorem would then assert fidelity for a federation with no model. A repeated variable INSIDE one scope is harmless: one constraint cannot split a cycle with itself.
attrs.prior_art: Fable 5, round-3 research pass. Fagin 1983 for the underlying Berge/α-β-γ distinction.
attrs.statement: The Berge sufficiency theorem requires constraints to be hyperedge INSTANCES: two constraints on the same scope from two sites are two constraint-nodes. A model that merges identical scopes into one hyperedge makes the theorem false.

attrs.evidence: Not proved. The two-hyperedge construction shows that sharing ≥2 variables is fatal, but a full characterization was not established.
attrs.statement: 'No split Berge cycle' is also NECESSARY for all-Γ sufficiency at arity > 2 (the analogue of FED-Q1-STARSTAR).

attrs.evidence: Membership witnesses are ONE-SIDED and the round-3 research pass claimed more for them than they carry. One satisfying assignment per admitted value proves M ⊆ true projection; nothing proves true projection ⊆ M. A site that under-reports its projection passes every membership check — demonstrated executably — and an omitted feasible value can manufacture a false empty message and hence a false UNSAT. Three distinct objects need distinguishing: a positive SAT certificate (constructive witnesses composing to a global assignment), an exact decision message (needs the exact projection), and a negative/UNSAT certificate (needs proof that excluded values are impossible, or an independently checkable local proof system). Directly relevant to TRVM/WRL-style continuous proof.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6 round-3 audit posed it; the round-4 audit found the direct neighbourhood. ATSERIAS, KOLAITIS & VARDI, "Constraint Propagation as a Proof System", CP 2004 (DOI 10.1007/978-3-540-30201-8_9) gives a sound-and-complete CSP refutation system over axioms, relational joins, projections and weakening, terminating in the empty relation — which is unusually close to what this claim asks for. Two routes follow. (a) TWO-SIDED BY CASES: for each v ∈ M a satisfying subtree assignment with x = v; for each v ∉ M a checkable refutation of subtree ∧ (x = v). Together those give M ⊆ truth AND truth ⊆ M. (b) NATIVE: a join/project derivation whose final derived unary relation IS M, so the verifier checks the relational proof rather than trusting a solver — this mirrors the separator algorithm itself instead of hiding it behind SAT, which is why it is the interesting one for TRVM/WRL. Alternatives to compare: SAT encoding with LRAT/DRAT refutations; pseudo-Boolean with VeriPB-style checking; OBDD representations, which Atserias–Kolaitis–Vardi also discuss.

attrs.evidence: The round-3 research pass proposed parameterizing the whole ledger over an ordered commutative monoid {zero, add, leq, convert}. THAT IS NOT ENOUGH FOR THIS LEDGER and is deliberately not implemented. `transfer` needs comparison, SUBTRACTION from a source account, and addition to a destination; a generic commutative monoid has no subtraction. A privacy-loss distribution composes under a monoid operation without having any meaningful "refund this PLD to the treasury". Two abstractions, not one: (A) an allocatable conserved resource, needing at least an ordered cancellative structure with a valid partial subtraction or residuation; (B) an irreversible information accountant, needing only zero / compose / admit-against-a-cap / conservative-guarantee, with no refund. Bridge them only where a real allocation notion exists. This may be cleaner than the current representation of privacy loss as double-entry value transferred to a sink.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6, rounds 3 and 4. The round-4 audit named the established neighbourhoods, which is what makes this searchable rather than a blank design question. FOR (A) THE CONSERVED ALLOCATABLE RESOURCE: separation algebras and cancellative partial commutative monoids; preordered partial commutative resource monoids; residuated and partially subtractive ordered monoids. A cancellative additive structure is the attractive one, because under its algebraic order a ≤ b supports a unique residual c with a + c = b where it exists — exactly the shape `transfer` needs. FOR (B) THE MONOTONE ACCOUNTANT: an ordered commutative monoid plus an admissible down-set/filter models composition without any refund; RDP at a fixed order is the canonical additive instance. DO NOT PICK A NAME BY ANALOGY — check that the exact total/partial operations and ordering laws match the kernel before adopting one.

attrs.evidence: PROOF. `admissibleTransfer(L,res,from,to,amt)` is the sole guard on `transfer`, which is the sole balance-mutating primitive among transfer/spend/refill/allocate/charge/use/repair. It requires `amt >= 0`, and for `kind[res] === 'irreversible'` it returns false when `from === SINK`. An accepted transfer therefore changes only `bal[from][res] -= amt` and `bal[to][res] += amt` with `amt >= 0` and `from !== SINK`; so `bal[SINK][res]` is touched only in the `to === SINK` case, where it increases by `amt >= 0`. Non-decreasing follows, and a transfer with `from === SINK` returns INFEASIBLE by the same clause. This is the proposition LED-C9 was reaching for and did not state: LED-C9 quantified over EVERY operation of the module, and `consolidate`/`forget` are operations of the module that are not transfer-mediated.

attrs.evidence: Reproduced. Privacy currencies are real-valued (ρ = Δ²/2σ²), so a real-valued instantiation needs rational or fixed-point amounts, or a tolerance in CB2. NOT FIXED in this round: it is a representation change to a shipped kernel and it was not required by any gate this round set. ROUND 3 narrowed the representation question and rejected one proposed answer. SOUND: exact rationals when the currency is rational; fixed-point with cost rounded UP and cap rounded DOWN is conservative for additive comparisons and never undercounts, while float64 admits unsoundly at a sub-resolution cap. NOT SOUND AS A UNIVERSAL ANSWER: "exact rationals" does not cover nonlinear conversions — log, sqrt, a minimum over RDP orders, PLD discretization — each of which needs its own directed/interval soundness argument. attrs.evidence: A terminology error worth correcting before it is encoded. By Rogers–Roth–Ullman–Vadhan 2016 a privacy FILTER is exactly a stopping rule that prevents exceeding a PRE-SPECIFIED budget; an ODOMETER tracks accumulated loss with no pre-specified budget. A fixed target with a stop is therefore a filter problem, and the filter theorems apply to it. THE REAL GAP IS DIFFERENT and is recorded separately: Feldman–Zrnic 2021 gives a clean adaptive filter at a FIXED RDP order α, and choosing the best α after seeing an adaptive transcript is a data-dependent choice the fixed-α theorem does not justify. That needs a simultaneous/multi-order filter theorem or a precommitment with a union argument — LED-RDP-ORDER.

attrs.evidence: SRC-BATES-2015-LPM. Linux Provenance Modules states G1 Complete as `the provenance record be gapless in its description of system activity`, scopes it to CONTROLLED DATA TYPES, and discharges it by placing a provenance hook directly beneath each LSM authorization hook and INHERITING LSM's separately verified complete mediation over that type universe. It declares the gap the placement creates — failed access attempts are not recorded — and relocates tamperproofness to secure boot and TPM attestation rather than closing it. SRC-SALTZER-1975-MEDIATION supplies the contrast: `every access to every object must be checked for authority` fixes no universe, and the universe is therefore a hypothesis of the principle rather than a consequence of it. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR R7.3: GPT-5.6 proposed keeping the ten-channel catalog as `descriptive coverage, not the theorem`. Half right. The catalog stops being the theorem — a count of channels was never evidence of closure, and one unmediated read gives none of it. But it does not become descriptive; it becomes THE THEOREM'S QUANTIFIER DOMAIN, and a universal over an under-declared domain is satisfiable by leaving things out of the domain. That is the sixth appearance of this artifact's recurring family, arriving one level above the fifth: R7.2 checked that a verdict was derived and not the derivation's INPUT; a mediation law with an unbound universe would check that every channel is mediated while nothing bounds the domain of `every`.

attrs.evidence: R5's gate inferred the obligation from the status: any claim at PROVED was allowed to satisfy ANY of {universal_affirmation, universal_refutation, existence}, and the consumption relation accepted the kind if it could discharge any one of them. GPT-5.6's audit reported that a universal PROVED claim therefore passes on a single constructive witness, or on a counterexample. The fix is the separation — `status` is an epistemic lifecycle state, `obligation` is the logical shape the support must establish — and all 75 settled claims (at INV-R7.5) now carry one, assigned by reading each statement rather than defaulted. `status_obligation_domain` still constrains which obligations are coherent with a status (a REFUTED claim may not claim universal_affirmation; a KNOWN claim is dischargeable only by cited_result), but it no longer supplies the obligation.

attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6 set EC-6's subject_quantity — an AUTHORITY test — to `bananas` and the gate exited 0; set it to `capability`, a real quantity but the wrong one, and the gate exited 0 again. The purest statement of it yet: THE RECORD CONTAINS THE SEMANTIC DISCRIMINATOR AND THE CHECKER CONFIRMS ONLY THAT NEARBY SYNTAX LOOKS VALID. Two rules close it. The subject must be a quantity declared in mosaic/operations.json — the CONSERVATION MATRIX's vocabulary, not a second list kept in the battery, so the two registries cannot drift into two accounts of one set of things. And the intervention must be able to REACH it: `authority_mutation` carries only `authority`, because perturbing an authority binding tells you nothing about capability. The first rule kills the nonsense, the second kills the swap, and both are registered mutations that run on every invocation.

attrs.evidence: R5 needed a tenth kind, `cited_result`, because the flat list could not represent a KNOWN claim — and GPT-5.6's audit reads that correctly as a symptom rather than a fix. The list mixes axes: `counterexample` is logical force, `measurement` is acquisition mode, `cited_result` is origin, `reproduction` is corroboration, `attestation` is provenance assurance, `model_judgment` is source class. An externally published theorem that this tree independently reproduces from an attested artifact is simultaneously cited, deductive, reproduced and attested; the current schema makes it pick one. THE FAMILIAR PART is that this is the Periodic Table's own problem one level up — TAX-COMPOUND found that most classified cells need two or more kinds, and TAX-FLOW concluded the likelier resolution is orthogonal AXES rather than a yes/no on a ninth kind. The evidence registry has now independently rediscovered the same shape, which is either a good sign about the shape or a bad sign about the habit.

attrs.evidence: The strict family is identity, conjunction introduction and elimination, and definitional EXPANSION — replacing a term by its registered definiens. The test for membership is that a checker can decide it by inspecting the rule's FORM. R6 implemented the family and the family immediately cost the artifact its only `is_ok`: ARG-LED-FILTER-ODOMETER-CITATION justified itself as "the object described satisfies the cited definition of X, therefore it is an X — premise and conclusion are deductively equivalent once the definition is fixed". The second clause is true and the first is where the work is. Deciding that a prose description falls under a definition is definitional SUBSUMPTION, it is defeasible, and no checker in this tree performs it. The terminator is now assumed_ok over ASM-FILTER-DEFN-SUBSUMPTION, and the strict family has zero members in use. A rule that changes nothing is a rule that is not enforcing.

settled_policy.why_refuted_is_settled: A REFUTED claim is ADJUDICATED — a construction that runs shows it false. It is settled in the sense this predicate means: the lane is no longer waiting on it. DECLARED, PROVISIONAL and OPEN are not.

statuses.CONDITIONAL: proved under a stated antecedent that is NOT discharged; the antecedent is in `assumptions`

statuses.MEASURED: an empirical count from a stated procedure, not a theorem
statuses.PROVED: a proof is given AND an executable check reproduces it here
statuses.PROVISIONAL: proposed on thin evidence, deliberately not promoted
statuses.REFUTED: shown false, with a construction that runs
